that is not built to compress: text under gzip runs about 3:1 to 8:1, JSON with repeated keys up to
about 60:1, and a log of near-identical lines into the low hundreds, while published bombs start
around 10,000:1. Neither key is under `[limits.hard]`, which bounds a value a request sets for
itself, and a request has no setting to lower them: the call's own arguments are that. **There is no spelling for an unbounded decompression**: not an
argument, since the largest `uint` is still clamped and `0` is a bound of zero; and not a
configuration, since `false` — which [`config/three-changeability-classes`](config.md#config-three-changeability-classes) reads as "no ceiling"
for the limits a request may raise — reads here as the shipped default, as a malformed value does. A
configuration that spells an unbounded decompression would be written once for a debugging session
and left in place.

A breach throws rather than truncating, because a truncated decompression that looks like success is
the failure this bound exists to prevent. The throw is a `ParseError` naming this rule, never an
`IOError`: a hostile archive and a failing disk are different questions, and a caller that cannot
tell them apart retries the one it should have refused. Its message names this rule, the half of
the bound that stopped the decode, and the two keys a call may lower. The bound is applied while the output grows
rather than to a buffer already allocated, so a bomb costs the ceiling and never the size its own
header claims.

`Core\Compress` and `Core\Zip` share this one rule, and `Core\Zip` applies it per entry *and* across
the archive — an archive whose entries are each within the bound and whose total is not is the same
attack one level up. This is why both classes are Tier 0 rather than sandboxed components
([`core-api/tier-roster`](core-api.md#core-api-tier-roster)): a sandboxed decoder gets a memory cap for free and this rule not at
all.

**The ceiling bounds what is held, and the ratio bounds what is spent.** A part a consumer inflates as
a stream and never holds — a spreadsheet sheet read row by row
([`core-classes/spreadsheet-reads-as-a-stream`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-reads-as-a-stream)) — is bounded by `input × ratio` alone, because
the request holds a window of it at any time and its CPU cap bounds the time. A part held whole keeps
both bounds, and an archive-wide total counts held parts only. The configured values reach a guest
the way `[image] max_pixels` does, clamped by the host before the call. Every `Core\Compress` and
`Core\Zip` member holds its output, so each keeps both bounds. A spreadsheet reader's message names
the part, the half of the bound that stopped it and the key that raises that half, and names no
rule: a program's caller reads it, and has no way to call with a lower bound. The PDF component's
`Reader::open`, `Reader::text` and `Pages::merge` decode every stream under both bounds, and the
attachments `Reader::open` holds count together against the ceiling. Their message has the
spreadsheet reader's shape. A stream's decode stops as its output grows, in the repository's patched
`hayro-syntax` (`vendor/hayro-syntax`), and an image's pixels are bounded by its dimensions instead.

A handler that decompresses something genuinely larger than the ceiling, such as a 200 MB archive
member, is refused until the operator raises `max_decompressed` for that deployment. The default is
chosen for the deployment that has not thought about it.

- **Memory:** the output buffer, at most the smaller of the two numbers, held by the request that
  asked for it. Nothing else outlives the call.

**Declined:**
- **An optional bound defaulting to unlimited, `?int $maxLength = null`.** The default of an optional
  bound is the whole decision, and `null` spells the wrong one.
- **The request's own `[limits] memory` as the only bound.** Reaching it stops the request and nothing
  catches that ([`errors/on-limit`](errors.md#errors-on-limit)), where a bomb should be an error the handler answers with a
  `400`. A heap ceiling also has no way to express a ratio.
- **A `Core\Compress\Bound` value object holding both numbers.** Two `uint` parameters carry the same
  two numbers without a class, a reference card and tests of their own.
- **Refusing early on the uncompressed size a frame or archive header declares.** The input's author
  wrote that number, so no member uses it, not even as a hint, and the output is measured as it grows.

<sub>See also [`core-api/tier-roster`](core-api.md#core-api-tier-roster), [`config/three-changeability-classes`](config.md#config-three-changeability-classes), [`programs/memory-priority`](programs.md#programs-memory-priority).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-image-pipeline"></a>

## An image is an immutable value carrying a plan, and nothing decodes until a terminal runs it

`rule:core-classes/image-pipeline`

An `Image` is an **immutable value**: the source bytes plus a plan. `open` keeps the bytes and calls
nothing, so bytes that are not an image throw at the terminal, and a pipeline costs one host-to-guest
call however it was built; every operation returns a new value that shares the bytes and extends the plan, so
branching a pipeline costs an array rather than a frame; and nothing decodes until a terminal —
`encode`, `variants`, `raw` — runs it. The plan executes in the order written, and steps may be fused
only where the result differs by resampling rounding alone.

That retires gd's mutable resource and every ambient mode flag with it: alpha always composites and
always saves, the resampling filter is an option on `resize`, and progressive encoding is an option
on `format`.

**The component's entry points are few, coarse and closed**, each one host-to-guest call carrying its
whole input and returning its whole output. There is no per-pixel, per-row or per-frame member, and
none is added later: `raw()` exports the whole buffer once for the caller that genuinely needs
pixels. The rule for any future entry point is a refusal — a member that would be called in a loop
over the image's own contents is not admitted, because its cost is the boundary rather than the work.
A call is a fixed cost and a bulk copy is memcpy-bound, and a pixel buffer is the largest thing a
request holds — a 24-megapixel frame is 96 MB at RGBA8 — so a request pays one instance and one
crossing per terminal, and the pixel buffer never leaves the guest. The builder grows a member
without touching the ABI, because a new operation is a new plan step rather than a new export.

**An animation moves through the plan as one value.** Every step runs on every frame, in the order
written, and the frames keep their delays. Only a GIF output keeps the frames: `encode` to GIF writes
every one with its delay, every other target writes the first frame, and `raw()` returns the first
frame. A plan whose output is not GIF decodes the first frame alone, so a thumbnail of an animation
costs one frame's decode, as a still image does. The pixel cap counts every frame the header states
either way ([`core-classes/image-pixel-cap`](core-classes.md#core-classes-image-pixel-cap)), so a request's pixel memory is bounded by the cap
however many frames it keeps. Every frame keeps one size: `trim` finds its box on the first frame
and crops every frame to it, and a `composite` overlay is made once and drawn on each. A GIF output
loops forever, since the decoders do not return the input's loop count.

A pipeline starts from one of four sources — encoded bytes (`open`), a blank canvas (`create`), RGBA8
pixels (`fromRaw`) or text set in a font (`measureText`) — and `run` returns one of three outputs: the
encoded file (`encode`), the RGBA8 pixels behind a size header (`raw`), or the size header alone
(`measureText`). An overlay is a row of the plan's flat overlay table that a `composite` step names by
position, because WIT has no recursive types. `hashDistance`, `Color` and `Font::fromBytes` are Novis
source and call no export.

`fromRaw` and `measureText` are pipeline starts, so each is a `source` case and not an export of its
own: both stay inside `run`, and a text source can be resized, padded and composited like any other
start. A `fromRaw` buffer that is not exactly `width * height * 4` bytes returns `invalid`, and the
pixel cap applies to `width * height` as it does to a header's declared size. A text source lays the
text out exactly as a `text` step does, so the size `measureText` returns is the box that step draws;
it rasterises the text to size it, which costs one glyph run. `run` returns `list<u8>` for every
output: the size header is width, then height, each a big-endian `u64`, and the host reads it into
the `Raw` shape or the size it returns. `hashDistance` counts the differing bits between two hashes
of one kind, which needs no decoder. A row's own `composite` steps name only earlier rows, so the
table is in dependency order and no overlay contains itself; the guest returns `invalid` for a
position that is not earlier, and the host flattens a nested Novis pipeline into rows when it builds
the plan.

- **Memory:** the `raw` output adds 16 bytes to the pixel buffer it returns.

A `Format` carries no members, because an enum declares only cases ([`enums/no-class-machinery`](enums.md#enums-no-class-machinery)):
`Image::mime(Format)` and `Image::extension(Format)` name a format's MIME type and file extension. The
plan's option shapes that the builder fills in for the caller — `format`'s, `rotate`'s and
`composite`'s — declare `x: ?T` rather than `x?: T` in `extensions/image/manifest.json`, because a
Novis shape has no way to leave a key out conditionally; both cross as the same WIT `option`.

**Partly on disk.** The interface is written: `wit/image.wit` holds package `nvs:image@1.0.0`, its
`codec` interface and the `image` world, and `crates/nvs-stdlib/tests/ext_world.rs` places every
builder member. A plan's `step` is a WIT record with one optional field per operation, exactly one
of them set, because the manifest tells a union's cases apart by their required keys and most steps
have none: a step crosses as a Novis array keyed by its operation, `['resize' => [...]]`. The
component's `run` and `variants` run every step, in order, and check each step's
options before anything is decoded; what each pixel step does beyond this rule, and the
pixel cap every frame a step makes is held to, are `extensions/image/src/ops.rs`'s module doc. A
`composite` step names only an earlier row, and one plan draws a bounded number of overlays counting
every level, so a few rows that each draw the one before twice cannot double the work per level
(`extensions/image/src/lib.rs` module doc). The builder's `composite` appends the overlay's own
rows and then the overlay to the table, renumbering the overlay's steps by the rows already there. `variants` decodes once and costs one host-to-guest call, counted by
`nvs_ext::call::Request::crossings` (`crates/nvs-ext/tests/image_pipeline.rs`). The `Novis\Image`
builder is Novis source in `extensions/image/nvs/`, packed into the component's `nvs.source`:
`Image` with every member `IMAGE_MEMBERS` in `crates/nvs-stdlib/tests/ext_world.rs` places, and
`Color` with `rgba` and `hex` and no named constants yet (`tests/conformance/novis/`). A canvas or
pixel source is held to the default pixel cap, not the `[image]` one. A plan that encodes a GIF
runs every step on every frame of a GIF, an APNG, an animated WebP, an AVIF image sequence and a
JPEG XL animation and writes them with their delays (`extensions/image/src/lib.rs`, `extensions/image/src/encode.rs`), and any other plan
decodes the first frame alone (`crates/nvs-ext/tests/image_pipeline.rs`).

The image world is called typed (`crates/nvs-ext/src/typed/image.rs`), so decoded pixels cross the
boundary in one copy each way, and their host bytes are charged to the request at their own size. A
`raw()` too large for the request stops at its memory limit (`crates/nvs-ext/src/call.rs`'s
`Request::run`).

**Declined:**
- **A gd-shaped handle with a call per operation.** It materialises every intermediate, prevents
  fusion, and either mutates in place, which no other Novis value does, or copies a frame per
  operation.
- **The resampling kernel at Tier 2, only the codecs in the sandbox.** It moves the pixel buffer
  across the boundary twice per pipeline, which costs more than the wasm penalty saves, and splits
  one job across two tiers. If a committed benchmark puts in-guest resampling far below native for a
  real workload, the exit is Tier 2 for that kernel alone, never `dlopen`.
- **ImageMagick or libvips compiled to wasm wholesale.** A surface that large is the long tail the
  component declines to own, and a C codebase that size is still one to build and audit inside the
  sandbox.
- **An export of its own for `fromRaw` and for `measureText`.** Each would carry the same input as a
  `source` case, add a boundary entry point for a job that is one more pipeline start, and break the
  closed export count.
- **A `variant` result for `run`.** It changes `run`'s signature to carry one case that two members
  use, where a size header on the same `list<u8>` carries it.
- **`hashDistance` as a call into the component.** It pays the boundary for a loop over a few bytes.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/image-pixel-model`](core-classes.md#core-classes-image-pixel-model), [`core-classes/image-pixel-cap`](core-classes.md#core-classes-image-pixel-cap), [`core-classes/image-one-entry-point-per-job`](core-classes.md#core-classes-image-one-entry-point-per-job).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-image-pixel-model"></a>

## Pixels are RGBA8 and nothing else, which retires gd's palettes, mode flags and drawing primitives

`rule:core-classes/image-pixel-model`

Pixels are **RGBA8**, straight alpha at the API, premultiplied where the maths needs it and never
visible to the caller. One model, and it retires whole families of gd concepts outright.

Palette images go: there is one truecolor model, a GIF is quantised on encode, and a colour is a
value rather than a palette index. Mode flags go, because there is no ambient state to hold them.
Per-pixel access goes, replaced by exporting the whole buffer once. Drawing primitives go entirely —
a rectangle is a blank canvas composited, text is a real font, and charts and diagrams are SVG on the
client; a shape layer is not planned, and a third-party extension may carry one. The affine matrix
members go, replaced by the four cases a web application reaches for, named: resize, rotate, flip,
crop. Screen and window capture go, a screen not being a request's business. Format detection by
positional array and integer constants goes, replaced by a typed header shape (`info`) and a format
enum whose MIME type and extension `Image::mime` and `Image::extension` give
([`core-classes/image-pipeline`](core-classes.md#core-classes-image-pipeline)). A resource to destroy goes, because an image is a value.

What this costs is that a program doing genuine raster drawing has no home here. That is deliberate:
the component exists to transform images a web application receives and produces, and every concept
above was priced against that.

What a gd program becomes, one row per concept:

| gd / exif | Novis |
|---|---|
| `imagecreatefrom*`, `imagecreatefromstring` | `Image::open`, the format detected from the bytes |
| `imagejpeg`, `imagepng`, `imagegif`, `imagewebp`, `imageavif` | `format(...)` then `encode()`; a path is written by the program from the result |
| `imagecopyresampled`, `imagecopyresized`, `imagescale`, `imagecrop`, `imagecropauto`, `imagerotate`, `imageflip`, `imagecopy`, `imagecopymerge` | `resize`, `crop`, `trim`, `rotate`, `flip`, `composite` |
| `imagefilter`, `imageconvolution`, `imagegammacorrect` | `sharpen`, `blur`, `grayscale`, `brightness`, `contrast`, `gamma`, `tint` |
| `imagettftext`, `imagefttext`, `imagettfbbox`, `imageftbbox` | `text`, `measureText` |
| `getimagesize*`, `imagesx`, `imagesy`, `exif_read_data`, `exif_imagetype`, `exif_thumbnail` | `Image::info`; a thumbnail is `resize` |
| `imagesetpixel`, `imagecolorat` | `raw()` and `fromRaw()`, once, the whole buffer |
| palettes, mode flags, drawing primitives, affine matrices, screen capture, gd's own formats | dropped, with the replacement above where one exists |

The component works on RGBA8 frames throughout, and a pixel source and the `raw`
output are RGBA8 rows (`extensions/image/src/lib.rs`). `Image::info` returns `exif` as the EXIF
block's fields of a JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF or JPEG XL input, the image's own IFDs without the
MakerNote, and `null` for a file with none (`extensions/image/src/info.rs`,
`crates/nvs-ext/tests/image_decode.rs`).

<sub>See also [`core-classes/image-pipeline`](core-classes.md#core-classes-image-pipeline), [`core-classes/image-format-roster`](core-classes.md#core-classes-image-format-roster).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-image-format-roster"></a>

## The format roster is a closed table of decoders and encoders, each naming what implements it

`rule:core-classes/image-format-roster`

The roster is a closed table, each row naming what decodes it, what encodes it, and what implements
both. JPEG, PNG with APNG, WebP, GIF and AVIF decode and encode. JPEG XL decodes only, because no
Rust encoder exists and the C library is not admitted. SVG and PDF decode only, by rasterisation.
TIFF, BMP, TGA, ICO, PNM, HEIC and gd's own formats do neither.

Each absence is a decision rather than an omission. HEIC is out because the codec is
patent-encumbered and has no Rust decoder, and iOS browsers upload JPEG by default. TIFF is a large
reader with a long CVE history, for a format web browsers do not display. gd's own formats are out
because nothing outside gd reads them. A third-party extension may carry any of them.

Every crate is pure Rust and on the licence allowlist, with exactly one C library — the lossy WebP
encoder — admitted because it runs only inside the sandbox. It is a build cost carried for one
feature, and it is dropped once a pure-Rust lossy WebP encoder exists. Resampling is
`fast_image_resize`, for its SIMD paths, and the guest is built with `simd128`
(`extensions/image/.cargo/config.toml`). AVIF encoding costs seconds of CPU per image and is
documented as queue work rather than a request-path call.

The image component's `run` decodes JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, AVIF and JPEG XL inside
the guest and refuses to encode JPEG XL (`crates/nvs-ext/tests/image_decode.rs`). AVIF decodes
through `rav1d` on one thread (`extensions/image/src/avif.rs`). JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF and AVIF
encode (`extensions/image/src/encode.rs`, `crates/nvs-ext/tests/image_pipeline.rs`): lossy WebP
through the libwebp that `extensions/image/build.rs` links, and AVIF through `ravif` on one thread.
`Image::info`'s `frames` is an animated input's real count, read off its header
(`extensions/image/src/info.rs`). Every frame of a GIF, an APNG, an animated WebP, an AVIF image
sequence and a JPEG XL animation decodes with its delay (`extensions/image/src/decode.rs`,
`extensions/image/src/avif.rs`). APNG is not encoded. SVG decodes through `resvg` with an image
resolver that reads only `data:` URIs and throws `RuntimeError` naming any other `href`
(`extensions/image/src/svg.rs`); its `<text>` is drawn with the twelve Liberation faces and never a
system font, in `Novis\Image` and in a `Novis\Pdf` render (`extensions/pdf/src/fonts.rs`). A
PDF page rasterises through `hayro` (`extensions/image/src/pdf.rs`).

<sub>See also [`core-classes/image-pipeline`](core-classes.md#core-classes-image-pipeline), [`core-classes/pdf-page-is-an-image-source`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-page-is-an-image-source), [`core-classes/image-pixel-cap`](core-classes.md#core-classes-image-pixel-cap).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-image-pixel-cap"></a>

## The pixel cap is read off the header before a buffer is allocated, and a call may only lower it

`rule:core-classes/image-pixel-cap`

Before any pixel buffer is allocated, the component reads the **declared** dimensions — width times
height, the declared canvas for an SVG, the selected page's box at the requested resolution for a
PDF — and refuses an image over `[image] max_pixels` with a throw naming the cap and the declared
size. A decompression bomb is refused from what the file claims, never discovered by exhausting
memory. An animation's cost is the sum of its frames: width times height times the frame count the
header states is held to the cap before any frame decodes, whether the plan decodes every frame or
the first one. One cap bounds a request however many frames a file claims, where a cap per frame
would let a thousand-frame file take a thousand frames.

It is a throw rather than a resource-limit fatal, because a rejected upload is an ordinary outcome
the application answers with a status code. A call may pass its own cap **only to lower** it, the
same monotone rule extension manifests take.

Bytes that are not an image the roster decodes throw a parse error; a codec fault beyond that is a
trap the sandbox contains, and it throws `ExtensionError` ([`packaging/a-guest-crash-throws`](packaging.md#packaging-a-guest-crash-throws)).

What it spends, per request that calls the component: the encoded input, at most two images at the
cap — source and result, 192 MB worst case at RGBA8, however the pixels split into frames — and the
encoded output, all charged to the
calling request's memory cap ([`packaging/a-guest-runs-under-the-requests-budget`](packaging.md#packaging-a-guest-runs-under-the-requests-budget)), and none of
which outlives the request. There are no threads in a guest, so a bulk import parallelises across
coroutines and cores rather than inside one call.

The cap is `[image] max_pixels`, the block's only key. It is `System` and reloads, and with nothing
written it is `"24M"`, read in the size grammar every other key of the file uses, so `M` is 2²⁰
pixels. `false` and zero are refused where they are written, because neither is a cap.

The key is `nvs_config::image` (`crates/nvs-config/tests/directives.rs`), and the image component's
`run` checks a header against a cap before it decodes, counting every frame of an animation
(`crates/nvs-ext/tests/image_decode.rs`). The
host sets every encoded source's `maxPixels` to the smaller of the call's and the key's value in the
request's snapshot before the call crosses (`nvs_ext::builtin::cap_pixels`), so the `{maxPixels}`
option of `Image::open` lowers the cap and never raises it
(`tests/conformance/novis/image-a-bomb-is-refused-before-it-is-decoded.nvst`).

<sub>See also [`core-classes/image-pipeline`](core-classes.md#core-classes-image-pipeline), [`core-classes/pdf-page-is-an-image-source`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-page-is-an-image-source), [`core-classes/spreadsheet-bulk-boundary`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-bulk-boundary).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-image-correct-by-default"></a>

## `open` orients and converts to sRGB, and `encode` strips metadata unless the plan kept it

`rule:core-classes/image-correct-by-default`

Three defaults make the common result the correct one.

`open` **applies the EXIF orientation**, so a phone photo is upright without the caller knowing the
tag exists. `open` **converts an embedded ICC profile to sRGB**, so a CMYK or wide-gamut JPEG resizes
to the colours the photographer saw; every pipeline is sRGB afterwards, and every encoder writes sRGB
without embedding a profile. Both are options that can be turned off by a caller who wants the raw
frame or the raw channels.

`encode` **strips metadata** — EXIF, XMP, IPTC, ICC — unless the plan explicitly kept it. Location
data in a re-encoded upload is the leak this default closes; a program that wants the tags reads them
from the header and stores them where it chooses. A kept EXIF block whose orientation `open` applied
is written with its orientation tag set to `1`, so a viewer does not turn the image a second time.

A profile that does not parse, or that is neither RGB nor CMYK, is ignored, as a browser ignores it:
the pixels are kept as decoded. A CMYK JPEG is read as Adobe stores it, inverted, whether its scan
is CMYK or YCCK.

An AVIF is oriented by its `irot` and `imir` boxes, which browsers follow, and an EXIF orientation
inside it is not applied a second time. A JPEG XL is oriented by its codestream's own field.

The component's `run` applies the orientation of a JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF or JPEG XL input,
converts its RGB profile to sRGB, and a JPEG's CMYK one too, and re-encodes JPEG,
PNG, WebP, GIF and AVIF with no metadata unless a `metadata` step keeps the EXIF block, which an
AVIF never carries (`extensions/image/src/decode.rs`, `extensions/image/src/avif.rs`,
`extensions/image/src/encode.rs`, `crates/nvs-ext/tests/image_pipeline.rs`). The `Novis\Image`
builder's `open` turns both on unless its options say `false`.

**Declined:**
- **Keep metadata by default, strip on request.** It is the least surprising default to someone who
  expects a resize to change nothing else. The surprising outcome it allows is a public thumbnail
  carrying a home address, and a default is the only place that outcome is prevented for every
  program rather than for the careful ones.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/image-pipeline`](core-classes.md#core-classes-image-pipeline), [`core-classes/image-one-entry-point-per-job`](core-classes.md#core-classes-image-one-entry-point-per-job).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-image-one-entry-point-per-job"></a>

## Comparison, hashing, placeholders, text, QR codes and SVG are one entry point each, because each is one job

`rule:core-classes/image-one-entry-point-per-job`

Beyond the pipeline, each remaining job is exactly one entry point.

**Comparison** decodes both inputs, refuses a size mismatch, and answers whether they are identical,
how many pixels differ, the maximum delta, a structural similarity score, and optionally a rendered
diff image for a test report. There is no assertion member: a composite assertion is an ordinary
method, so a test asserts on the comparison's own numbers and the failure ledger records it.
**Perceptual, difference and average hashing** plus a distance function serve near-duplicate
detection. **Placeholders** and **palette extraction** serve the front end.

**Text** renders over a font supplied as bytes, with no system font lookup, since the guest has no
filesystem. It is shaped by `harfrust` in runs the Unicode bidirectional algorithm orders, so
ligatures, Arabic joining, Indic conjuncts and right-to-left lines are drawn as the font defines
them. **QR codes** are one entry point, because a QR code is an image a web application
produces daily. **SVG** is an input format whose declared canvas counts against the pixel cap and
whose scripts and foreign objects are ignored. An image inside it is read only from a `data:` URI,
and **an external reference throws** `RuntimeError` naming it, because there is nothing in the guest
to resolve one with. Rasterising is how an uploaded SVG is displayed safely; sanitising one would be
the repair that is refused everywhere else.

Comparison is the component's `compare` export, whose module doc
`extensions/image/src/compare.rs` says what a delta is and how the SSIM and the rendered diff are
made, and `Image::compare` returning a `Diff` in `extensions/image/nvs/`, which compares an `Image`
with no `format` step as PNG so no lossy re-encode moves a pixel (`crates/nvs-ext/tests/image_analysis.rs`,
`tests/conformance/novis/`). Hashing is the component's `hash` export, whose module
doc `extensions/image/src/hash.rs` defines the three kinds, each its own fixed length so two kinds
never compare, and is written in the component with no hashing crate linked; `Image::hash` and
`Image::HashKind`; and `Image::hashDistance` as Novis source, counting differing bits and throwing a
`LogicError` for two lengths. Placeholders and the palette are the component's
`placeholder` and `palette` exports, whose module doc `extensions/image/src/summary.rs` defines
both placeholder formats and how the palette clusters `color_quant`'s colours, and
`Image::placeholder`, `Image::PlaceholderKind` and `Image::palette`. QR codes are the
component's `qr` export over the `qrcode` crate, whose module doc `extensions/image/src/qr.rs`
says how `size`, `margin` and the level make the image and what each default is, and
`QrCode::render` and `QrCode::Level`; the host checks read each code back with `rqrr`. Text is
the `text` step and the `text` source, shaped by `harfrust` and drawn by `ab_glyph`, whose
module doc `extensions/image/src/text.rs` says how a size, a line, shaping, `maxWidth` and `align` set the
text and what the box is, and `Image::text`, `Image::measureText` and `Font::fromBytes`, which
checks only the file's first four bytes and calls no export. SVG decodes through `resvg` with an
image resolver that reads only `data:` URIs (`extensions/image/src/svg.rs`), and
`crates/nvs-ext/tests/image_decode.rs` and
`tests/conformance/novis/image-an-svg-opens-as-an-image.nvst` throw for a path and an address.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/image-pipeline`](core-classes.md#core-classes-image-pipeline), [`core-classes/image-pixel-cap`](core-classes.md#core-classes-image-pixel-cap), [`testing/assertions-are-typed`](testing.md#testing-assertions-are-typed).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-image-barcode-roster"></a>

## `Novis\Image\Barcode` renders eight 1D and DataMatrix symbologies, and a code and a QR code render as SVG

`rule:core-classes/image-barcode-roster`

`Novis\Image\Barcode` renders **Code 128, GS1-128, EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, Code 39, ITF-14 and
DataMatrix**, chosen by `Barcode::Symbology`, each as an SVG string or as any raster format the
component encodes. QR codes stay `Novis\Image\QrCode`'s, which gains SVG output too.

| Member | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Barcode::render(string $data, Barcode::Symbology $symbology, ?{height?: uint, module?: uint, margin?: uint, text?: bool, format?: Format} $options = null): bytes` | the code as an encoded image, PNG by default |
| `Barcode::svg(string $data, Barcode::Symbology $symbology, ?{height?: uint, module?: uint, margin?: uint, text?: bool} $options = null): string` | the code as an SVG document |
| `QrCode::svg(string $data, ?{margin?: uint, level?: QrCode::Level} $options = null): string` | a QR code as an SVG document |
| `QrCode::giroCode({name: string, iban: string, amount?: decimal, bic?: string, reference?: string, text?: string}): string` | the EPC payment text (GiroCode) a banking app reads, for `QrCode::render` or `QrCode::svg` |

A wrong check digit, or a character the symbology cannot carry, throws `LogicError` naming it; a code
is never repaired by computing a digit the program did not write. `giroCode` checks the IBAN's checksum
and the field lengths the EPC layout fixes, and is Novis source: the payload is text, so it needs no
crossing. SVG output is vector, so a code in a PDF prints sharp at any size; it is the one form a PDF
document needs ([`core-classes/pdf-one-engine`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-one-engine)).

The 1D codes are `barcoders` and DataMatrix is `datamatrix`, both pure Rust in the image component's
sandbox. Every code a test writes is read back by a reader that is a dev-dependency of the test only.

- **Memory:** a code is at most a few thousand modules, so a render is far under the pixel cap.

The `barcode` export draws every symbology, `qr` writes `svg`, and `Barcode`,
`QrCode::svg` and `QrCode::giroCode` are in the binary. `extensions/image/src/barcode.rs` says what
each symbology takes and what each option's default is. `crates/nvs-ext/tests/image_barcode.rs`
reads every code back with `rxing`, and `crates/nvs-cli/tests/image_barcode.rs` pins the GiroCode
layout.

**Declined:**
- **PDF417 and Aztec.** Each is a large encoder for documents almost no web application produces.
- **A barcode reader.** Reading a code from a photo is a computer-vision job, outside a codec
  component.
- **Computing a missing check digit.** The program wrote a number; the code carries that number or
  throws.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/image-one-entry-point-per-job`](core-classes.md#core-classes-image-one-entry-point-per-job), [`core-classes/image-format-roster`](core-classes.md#core-classes-image-format-roster), [`core-classes/pdf-one-engine`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-one-engine).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-intl-roster"></a>

## `Novis\Intl` is eight classes, one per job, over one manifest class, and message formatting is not in it

`rule:core-classes/intl-roster`

The intl component's classes are `Collator`, `NumberFormat`, `PluralRules`, `DateFormat`,
`RelativeTime`, `ListFormat`, `Segmenter` and `Locale`, all under `Novis\Intl` and written in Novis
source over one manifest class, `Novis\Intl\Icu`, whose static methods are the exports of
`nvs:intl/icu` in `wit/intl.wit`.

| Class | Members |
|---|---|
| `Collator` | `sort`, `sortKeys` — the strings in the locale's order, or one byte key per string that orders the same way |
| `NumberFormat` | `decimal`, `percent`, `currency`, `compact` |
| `PluralRules` | `cardinal`, `ordinal` — each returns `Core\Cldr::PluralCategory` |
| `DateFormat` | `dateTimes`, `dates`, `times` — over `Core\Time\DateTime`, `Date` and `TimeOfDay` |
| `RelativeTime` | `format` — a count and a `RelativeTime::Unit`, negative in the past |
| `ListFormat` | `join` — "and", "or" and unit lists |
| `Segmenter` | `words`, `sentences` |
| `Locale` | `negotiate`, `resolve` |

Their signatures are the classes in `extensions/intl/nvs/`, and their options shapes and enums are
`wit/intl.wit`'s. No member reaches another's job, and there is no per-value member beside a batch one
([`core-api/one-paradigm-per-operation`](core-api.md#core-api-one-paradigm-per-operation)). Message formatting is not in the roster until ICU4X's
MessageFormat 2 is stable, and grapheme segmentation, case mapping and normalization stay in `Core\Str`.

A manifest names exactly one class, so `Icu` is the boundary and the job classes a program uses are
Novis source in the same `.nvsx`, as the image component's are. The Novis half does the two things the
guest cannot: it converts a `Core\Time` value to local fields ([`core-classes/intl-host-converts-time`](core-classes.md#core-classes-intl-host-converts-time)),
and it writes a number as its decimal text.

- **Two collation members, two results.** `sort` returns the strings in order; `sortKeys` returns bytes
  a program stores in a column or sorts rows by. A key is valid only under the ICU4X version the
  component pins, so a stored key is rebuilt when the binary's component version changes.
- **A number crosses as its decimal text.** The text is exact, so a `decimal` amount is never rounded
  through `f64`, and the export has one numeric type. A `float` that is not finite throws
  `RuntimeError` in the Novis half before the call, and a currency code that is not three ASCII letters
  throws `LogicError`. The four `NumberFormat` members are four styles with four options shapes.
- **One plural category type.** A catalog keyed on `Core\Cldr`'s category reads `PluralRules`'s with no
  conversion.

`Core\Cldr::pluralCategory` and `ordinalCategory` stay in Tier 0 beside `PluralRules`. On a bare
language tag from `Core\Cldr`'s roster the two return the same category for every number; `PluralRules`
also reads a region, so `pt-PT` may differ from `Core\Cldr`'s `pt`. Neither is deprecated: `Core\Cldr`
is the one a template reaches without the sandbox, and `PluralRules` is the one that knows every
locale.

- **Memory:** nothing until a process first calls the component; then the compiled module, shared by
  every core, and each calling request's instance under that request's cap. The CLDR data is in the
  binary, and the component's module doc states its size. If that size is too large, the answer is a
  slimmer locale set, never an optional component.

The component crate is `extensions/intl/`, its Novis half is `extensions/intl/nvs/`, and `wit/intl.wit`
is the interface it exports.

**Declined:**

- **Numbers as a `variant` of `s64`, `f64` and digits.** It adds three cases to every numeric export to
  carry what one string already carries exactly.
- **`RelativeTime` from a `Duration`.** A month and a year are not a fixed number of nanoseconds, so the
  unit would be a guess. The program chooses the unit and the count.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/intl-batch-shape`](core-classes.md#core-classes-intl-batch-shape), [`core-classes/intl-locale-is-an-argument`](core-classes.md#core-classes-intl-locale-is-an-argument), [`core-classes/intl-host-converts-time`](core-classes.md#core-classes-intl-host-converts-time), [`packaging/the-first-party-components-are-built-in`](packaging.md#packaging-the-first-party-components-are-built-in), [`programs/framework-core-half`](programs.md#programs-framework-core-half).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-intl-batch-shape"></a>

## Every `Novis\Intl` member but `Locale::negotiate` takes a list and returns a list, in one locale and one crossing

`rule:core-classes/intl-batch-shape`

Every `Novis\Intl` member except `Locale::negotiate` takes a list and returns a list of the same length
in the same order, and makes exactly one host-to-guest call. A single value is a list of one, at the
same one call, so sorting 10,000 names or formatting a page of prices costs one crossing and one copy
each way ([`packaging/the-boundary-is-the-cost`](packaging.md#packaging-the-boundary-is-the-cost)).

One call has one locale. A program whose rows carry different locales makes one call per locale, which
is the shape it has anyway when it groups output by reader. A per-item locale would put a string per
item into every crossing, for a case no web page has.

`negotiate` is the one exception, because its input is one `Accept-Language` header from one request,
and a batch of headers is not a thing a request holds.

The interface holds the shape: every export of `nvs:intl/icu` but `negotiate` takes a `list` as its
first parameter and returns a `list`, and `crates/nvs-stdlib/tests/ext_world.rs` fails naming an export
that does not. `Collator::sort`'s export returns the strings' positions, so only numbers cross back and
the Novis half reorders the list it already has; equal strings keep their input order.

- **Memory:** a batch costs its input and its output, copied once each way. A large batch is bounded by
  the request's memory cap like any other value.

**Declined:**

- **A comparator for collation.** A sort of 10,000 strings would make about 130,000 crossings.
- **A per-value member beside each batch member.** It is a second way to reach every operation, and
  saves only a pair of brackets.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/intl-roster`](core-classes.md#core-classes-intl-roster), [`packaging/the-boundary-is-the-cost`](packaging.md#packaging-the-boundary-is-the-cost), [`packaging/a-value-crosses-as-its-wit-type`](packaging.md#packaging-a-value-crosses-as-its-wit-type).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-intl-locale-is-an-argument"></a>

## A `Novis\Intl` locale is always an argument: a malformed tag throws, and an unknown one falls back along CLDR's chain

`rule:core-classes/intl-locale-is-an-argument`

Every `Novis\Intl` member takes its locale as a BCP 47 tag argument. There is no default locale, no
setting that holds one and no `[intl]` configuration block ([`core-api/no-ambient-state`](core-api.md#core-api-no-ambient-state)).

- **A malformed tag** throws `LogicError` naming it, cut to its first 64 characters. A locale is the
  program's own data, so a bad one is a bug.
- **A well-formed tag with no data** falls back along CLDR's chain — `de-AT` to `de`, and at last to
  the root locale — and formats. It never throws: a tag a program got from a user or a header is
  well-formed and unknown far more often than it is wrong.
- **`Locale::resolve`** returns, for each tag and a `Locale::Service`, the locale whose data answers: `de` for
  `de-XX`, `und` where only the root does. Coverage differs between services, so the service is an
  argument. It is how a program learns which locale answered.
- **A `-u-` keyword that an option also names** — `ks`, `kf` or `kn` beside `strength`, `caseFirst`
  or `numeric` — throws `LogicError`, so no option has two spellings. A keyword no option names, such
  as `co`, `nu`, `ca` or `hc`, is read from the tag, so a user's preference travels with their locale.

`Locale::negotiate` never throws for its header: an empty, malformed or unmatched `Accept-Language`
returns the default, because the header is request data the program does not control. It matches each
range against the offered tags with CLDR's fallback and returns the offered tag as the program spells
it. Only the first 32 ranges are read, which keeps a hostile header's cost fixed; no browser sends a
tenth of that. A malformed tag among the offered locales or the default throws `LogicError`, because
those are the program's.

**Declined:**

- **A default locale** — a setting, a per-request value, or the current request's `Accept-Language`
  read implicitly. Each is ambient state.
- **Throwing for an unknown but well-formed locale.** A page that throws for `gsw` is worse than one in
  German.

<sub>See also [`core-api/no-ambient-state`](core-api.md#core-api-no-ambient-state), [`core-classes/intl-roster`](core-classes.md#core-classes-intl-roster), [`security/no-cross-request-state`](security.md#security-no-cross-request-state).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-intl-host-converts-time"></a>

## A `Core\Time\DateTime` reaches the intl guest as local fields, an offset and a zone id, and the guest has no time-zone database

`rule:core-classes/intl-host-converts-time`

`DateFormat::dateTimes` converts each `Core\Time\DateTime` in Novis, with `Core\Time`, to the record
`local-date-time` of `wit/intl.wit` — year, month, day, hour, minute, second, nanoseconds, the UTC
offset in seconds and the IANA zone id — and the guest formats those fields. `Core\Time` owns the
time-zone database, and the binary carries one.

`DateFormat::dates` and `times` cross as `nvs:ext/types`' `date` and `time-of-day` records, which are
local fields already. A `DateTime` does not cross as the `date-time` record, because that record is an
instant and a zone name, and turning it into fields is the time-zone database's job. An `Instant` is
placed in its zone with `Core\Time` first; a member that took an `Instant` and a `Zone` would be a
second way to write `dateTimes`.

The guest names a zone from its id and offset: `DateFormat::ZoneStyle::Offset`, `Location` or
`Generic`. A zone's
specific daylight-time name is not offered, because it needs to know whether the offset is daylight
time. The calendar is the locale's, selected by a tag's `-u-ca-` keyword; the fields cross as ISO
fields and the guest converts them.

**Declined:**

- **A second time-zone database in the guest**, so that a `DateTime` crosses as its instant. It doubles
  data `Core\Time` already carries, and two databases can disagree about the same instant.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/intl-roster`](core-classes.md#core-classes-intl-roster), [`packaging/a-value-crosses-as-its-wit-type`](packaging.md#packaging-a-value-crosses-as-its-wit-type).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-pdf-render-has-no-io"></a>

## `Novis\Pdf` is a built-in component that performs no I/O, and an asset it cannot resolve throws

`rule:core-classes/pdf-render-has-no-io`

PDF generation is the third built-in component ([`packaging/the-first-party-components-are-built-in`](packaging.md#packaging-the-first-party-components-are-built-in)):
everything a program names is under `Novis\Pdf`, present in every binary, and run in the sandbox with
no grant. It is not `Core`: a layout engine, a font parser and image codecs unsandboxed in every request
would contradict the reason the image component is a component. It is not native: nothing in it holds
state or privilege past one request.

**The component performs no I/O of any kind.** Every asset a document uses — images, stylesheets beyond
the inline ones, fonts, and PDFs placed as pages — crosses the boundary as bytes in a caller-supplied
map, and a reference in the HTML, the CSS or an inline SVG resolves against that map and nothing else. A
`data:` URI decodes in place, because its bytes are already in the document. A `file:` or `http(s):`
URL, an absolute path, or a name the map lacks **throws** `LogicError` naming it, rather than rendering
a broken-image gap: a generated document must be deterministic, and refusing beats repairing. A program
that wants a remote image fetches it itself, under the outbound policy, and passes the bytes.

The class of exploit that defines HTML-to-PDF rendering — server-side request forgery and local file
read through an `<img src>` — is thereby absent by construction: there is nothing to trick into
fetching, because there is no fetching. The guest needs no clock either: a date in the document is text
the program wrote, and the file carries a creation time only when the program passes one
([`core-classes/pdf-output-is-inert`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-output-is-inert)). HTML, CSS, fonts, images and SVG are still hostile bytes. The
request's memory cap and deadline contain them, the HTML is held to the parser's element cap
([`core-classes/html-parsing`](core-classes.md#core-classes-html-parsing)), and the component adds **no limit of its own**: a bulk or slow
render belongs in `Core\Queue`.

The component's fixtures hold it: a render with **no capability grants** that succeeds, so the no-I/O
claim is demonstrated rather than asserted; a `file:///…` reference, an `http:` URL and a name absent
from the asset map, each in HTML, CSS and SVG and each throwing, with no network or filesystem access
observable from the guest; and a `data:` image that renders.

- **Memory:** per rendering request, the HTML, the asset map, the layout tree and the output document,
  all inside the request's memory cap and freed when the request ends. A program that never renders
  pays nothing.

`extensions/pdf/src/assets.rs` resolves every reference in HTML, CSS and inline SVG against the map
and `data:` before anything is laid out, and throws for the rest. `crates/nvs-ext/tests/pdf.rs`
renders with no grant, and a `file:`, `http:` and unknown name each throw there and in
`tests/conformance/novis/pdf-a-missing-asset-throws.nvst`. `extensions/pdf/tests/render.rs` throws
for each in a linked stylesheet, its `url()`s and an SVG `<image>` or `<use>`.

**Declined:**
- **`Core`.** A layout engine, a font parser and image decoders would sit unsandboxed in every binary
  and every in-flight request.
- **Native.** Nothing here needs a connection lifetime or a runtime privilege, and the sandbox is the
  feature rather than a cost to route around.
- **Leaving the category to the third-party channel.** That produces incompatible libraries with
  disjoint CSS subsets, and the popular ones fetch whatever the HTML names, which is the category's
  vulnerability class. One first-party no-I/O way to do the job prevents both.
- **A fetch hook or an allow-list of hosts.** It brings back the fetching this rule removes, and a
  program already fetches under its own outbound policy.
- **A render limit of its own.** A render is a request's work, priced by the request's memory cap and
  deadline like any other; a second knob would be one more number to tune with no new bound behind it.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/pdf-roster`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-roster), [`core-classes/pdf-one-engine`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-one-engine), [`core-classes/pdf-output-is-inert`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-output-is-inert), [`core-classes/spreadsheet-has-no-io`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-has-no-io).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-pdf-roster"></a>

## `Novis\Pdf` is `Document`, `Page`, `Rendered`, `Pages` and `Reader`, with `Engine` the manifest class

`rule:core-classes/pdf-roster`

`Novis\Pdf` is five classes a program names — `Document` renders, `Page` is one page's facts, `Rendered`
is a render's result, `Pages` merges and `Reader` reads — and `Engine`, the manifest class whose static
methods are the WIT exports (`wit/pdf.wit`), the way `Novis\Image\Codec` is the image component's.

| Member | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Document::fromHtml(Core\Html\Markup\|string $html): Document` | the document to render |
| `->asset(string $name, bytes $data): Document` | adds one named asset ([`core-classes/pdf-render-has-no-io`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-render-has-no-io)) |
| `->header(callable $fn, ?{height?: string} $options = null): Document` | a function from `Page` to `Core\Html\Markup`, drawn in the top margin of each page ([`core-classes/pdf-header-is-a-page-function`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-header-is-a-page-function)) |
| `->footer(callable $fn, ?{height?: string} $options = null): Document` | the same, in the bottom margin |
| `->slots(callable $fn): Document` | a function from `Page` to an `array<Core\Html\Markup>` keyed by slot name, filling each `<slot name>` in a repeated table row ([`core-classes/pdf-tables-across-pages`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-tables-across-pages)) |
| `->standard(Document::Standard $standard): Document` | `PdfA2b`, `PdfA3b` or `PdfUa1` ([`core-classes/pdf-standards-and-passwords`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-standards-and-passwords)) |
| `->invoiceXml(string $xml): Document` | the Factur-X XML ([`core-classes/pdf-factur-x-is-the-one-attachment`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-factur-x-is-the-one-attachment)) |
| `->password(string $password): Document` | encrypts the output with AES-256 |
| `->created(Core\Time\Instant $at): Document` | the creation time in the metadata; absent, the file has none |
| `->render(): Rendered` | one render: one call, two with a header, footer or slot function |
| `Page->number`, `->count`, `->isFirst()`, `->isLast()`, `->name` | the page's number from 1, the document's page count, and its named page or `null` |
| `Page->string(string $name): ?string` | the page's `string-set` value |
| `Page->marks(string $name): array<string>`, `->marksUpTo(string $name): array<string>` | the `data-mark` values on this page, and on every page up to it |
| `Rendered->bytes`, `->pageCount` | the file and its page count |
| `Rendered->dropped`, `->missingGlyphs`, `->overflows` | what the render could not do ([`core-classes/pdf-css-subset`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-css-subset)) |
| `Pages::of(bytes $pdf, ?array<uint> $pages = null): Pages`, `Pages::merge(array<Pages> $parts): bytes` | merging, splitting and reordering ([`core-classes/pdf-reader-and-merge`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-reader-and-merge)) |
| `Reader::open(bytes $pdf): Reader`, `->pageCount`, `->metadata`, `->attachments()`, `->invoiceXml()`, `->text(uint $page): string` | reading a PDF |

`Document` is a value: each method returns a new `Document`, so a base document with its assets and
footer is shared and varied without one render changing another. `Standard` is declared in
`Document`, the one class that uses it ([`enums/an-enum-lives-in-the-class-that-uses-it`](enums.md#enums-an-enum-lives-in-the-class-that-uses-it)).
`Page` and `Rendered` are made only by the component.

**The errors**, each naming what it refuses:

| Throws | When |
|---|---|
| `LogicError` | a reference the asset map does not resolve; a broken standard; an invoice XML outside PDF/A-3b; a password beside a PDF/A standard; a page number outside its document in `Pages::of` or `Reader::text` |
| `ParseError` | a source PDF, font or image that does not parse; an encrypted source PDF; an invoice XML that is not well-formed |
| `RuntimeError` | page numbers that do not settle after five layout passes (`target-counter()`, `counter(pages)`) |

The request's memory cap and deadline end a render that exceeds them as they end any call.

- **Memory:** a `Document` holds its HTML and its assets until it is freed; the render's own memory is
  [`core-classes/pdf-render-has-no-io`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-render-has-no-io)'s.

**On disk.** `extensions/pdf/manifest.json` declares `Engine` and `Standard`, and
`extensions/pdf/nvs/` holds `Document`, `Page`, `Rendered`, `Pages` and `Reader`.

**Declined:**
- **A `Pdf` facade with static `render($html, $options)`.** The options a render takes — assets, three
  functions, a standard, a password — are an options bag too large to read, and a base document could
  not be shared.
- **`data-mark-<name>` attributes.** The editor completes fixed attribute names only, so one
  `data-mark="name:value"` attribute is what completes and explains itself.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/pdf-render-has-no-io`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-render-has-no-io), [`core-classes/pdf-header-is-a-page-function`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-header-is-a-page-function), [`core-classes/pdf-reader-and-merge`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-reader-and-merge), [`core-api/options-bag`](core-api.md#core-api-options-bag).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-pdf-one-engine"></a>

## The only input language is HTML plus a CSS subset, and one engine of our own over Rust crates renders it

`rule:core-classes/pdf-one-engine`

The sole input language is **HTML plus the CSS subset plus inline SVG**, and there is one engine. A
program builds a document the way it builds a page: with ``html`…` `` templates
([`core-classes/html-template`](core-classes.md#core-classes-html-template)) that compose by concatenation before a single render call. There is
no Novis-side builder of headings and tables, because a template already is one.

There is no second, imperative engine with its own coordinate model. That would be two ways to write
one job, and a program that owns both a DOM-based renderer and a coordinate-based one maintains two
layouts of every page. Drawings are inline SVG, the same answer the image component gives for charts,
and an existing PDF's page is placed with `<img>` ([`core-classes/pdf-reader-and-merge`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-reader-and-merge)).

The HTML is parsed by the same crate the language's own parser uses
([`core-classes/html-parsing`](core-classes.md#core-classes-html-parsing)), the patched copy under `vendor/html5ever`, compiled into the
sandbox rather than linked natively, so the language and its PDF component parse HTML identically and
under the same element cap.

No HTML paged-media engine exists to link as a library, so the engine is **our own cascade, layout and
pagination** over production Rust crates: `cssparser` and `selectors` for the cascade, `parley` over
`harfrust` and `skrifa` for text, with `fontique`'s system font discovery off, `hypher` for
hyphenation, `taffy` for flex and grid, `usvg` and `krilla-svg` for SVG, `hayro` through `krilla`'s
`pdf` feature for placed pages, and `krilla` for the file. The pagination layer nobody ships is ours to
write. A crate that does not build for `wasm32-wasip2` is replaced by its nearest pure-Rust equivalent,
and this paragraph names the replacement. The rules on this component are written against the
interface, not the crates, so a production-grade paged-media crate may replace the assembled engine
wholesale and must still meet them.

- **Memory:** per request that renders, the HTML, the asset map, the layout tree and the output
  document, all inside the request's memory cap, none of it outliving the request. Wall-clock is
  milliseconds for an invoice and seconds for a long report, so a bulk or slow render belongs in the
  queue.
- **Depth.** Table cells and flex and grid items are each laid out by a call inside the one around
  them, so their nesting is bounded at 32 levels (`MAX_DEPTH` in `extensions/pdf/src/layout/text.rs`).
  A document nested deeper throws `LogicError` naming the bound. A level costs about 21 KiB of the
  component's stack in a release build, and the stack is 2 MiB (`extensions/pdf/.cargo/config.toml`),
  twice the target's default, so the deepest document leaves more than half free. The larger stack
  spends 1 MiB more linear memory per render. Plain blocks and inline-blocks are laid out without
  recursing and need no bound, and the parser's element cap already flattens anything past 512 open
  elements.
- **Limits.** Three inputs grow the work with their size and end at the request's memory limit (128
  MiB by default), which throws as every guest that reaches it does ([`packaging/a-guest-crash-throws`](packaging.md#packaging-a-guest-crash-throws)):
  one word of two million characters, 100,000 nested `div`s (flattened into siblings; 50,000 render
  under the default, and time grows linearly), and a page whose content stream saves its state a
  million times when its text is read. No bound below the memory limit is fairer, because each costs
  what it asks for. The attacks under `tests/hostile/novis/Pdf-Document/fromHtml/` and
  `tests/hostile/novis/Pdf-Reader/text/02-a-page-that-saves-its-state.nvs` pin them with
  `ends-early`.

**On disk.** `extensions/pdf/` parses with the patched `html5ever` under the same cap,
computes styles with its cascade over `cssparser` and `selectors`, shapes with `parley`, hyphenates
with `hypher`, lays out flex and grid with `taffy`, draws inline SVG with `usvg` and `krilla-svg`,
places existing pages through `krilla`'s `pdf` feature and reads them with `hayro-interpret`, and
writes with `krilla` (`extensions/pdf/Cargo.toml`). Pagination is `extensions/pdf/src/paginate/`.

**Declined:**
- **A Novis-side document builder** that appends headings, tables and page breaks and emits HTML. It
  is a second way to write what a template already writes, and every element it knows is one more
  name to learn and keep in step with the subset.
- **A headless-browser backend**, opt-in or default. It is a browser process per render, hundreds of
  megabytes outside any request's attribution, with its own sandbox and lifecycle to operate, and it
  fetches whatever the HTML names. A document the subset cannot reach is written in the subset, or
  rendered by a program outside Novis.
- **An engine written in Novis.** It would be a second, unfuzzed implementation of shaping, bidi, line
  breaking, cascade and layout, buying nothing the wasm build does not already give.
- **A first-party imperative PDF API.** The first-party answer to drawing at a coordinate is HTML, CSS
  and SVG; a third-party package may carry one.
- **`fulgur` or WeasyPrint as a dependency.** `fulgur` has the same design and is young, and WeasyPrint
  is Python; both are references and test comparisons only.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/pdf-render-has-no-io`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-render-has-no-io), [`core-classes/pdf-css-subset`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-css-subset), [`core-classes/html-parsing`](core-classes.md#core-classes-html-parsing), [`core-classes/html-template`](core-classes.md#core-classes-html-template).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-pdf-css-subset"></a>

## The render result lists every declaration and element it dropped, every missing glyph and every overflow

`rule:core-classes/pdf-css-subset`

The engine implements a **documented subset** of CSS ([`core-classes/pdf-css-subset-table`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-css-subset-table)) and
handles everything outside it by CSS's own forward-compatible parsing: an unknown declaration is
dropped, never guessed at.

What this rule adds to that standard behaviour is **visibility**. `Rendered::dropped` lists every
declaration the engine dropped with its property, value, selector and source position, so a test
asserts the list is empty and a document that silently depends on unsupported CSS cannot survive CI.
"Renders fine in the browser, wrong in the PDF" is the failure an invisible drop produces, and a visible
list is what turns it into a test. The same holds for content: an element the subset does not render
(`<iframe>`, `<video>`, `<canvas>`, a form field) is listed and drawn as nothing, and `<script>` never
runs and is not listed, because no program expects it to run in a document.

Three other things a render cannot do are **reported, never thrown**, because the document is still
correct apart from them and a throw would lose the whole file over one character:

- a character no font in the chain has is drawn as the font's empty box and listed in
  `Rendered::missingGlyphs` with the fonts it tried ([`core-classes/pdf-default-fonts`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-default-fonts));
- markup in a margin, a header, a footer or a slot taller than its area is listed in
  `Rendered::overflows` with its page ([`core-classes/pdf-header-is-a-page-function`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-header-is-a-page-function));
- a declaration the subset lists with a value it does not take is dropped and listed like an unknown
  one.

The component's fixtures owe a fixture using an unsupported property that renders with that property
in the dropped list, and a clean fixture whose three lists are empty.

**On disk.** `extensions/pdf/src/css/` is the cascade, and `Rendered::dropped` lists what it
drops with its selector and position, and each element the subset does not render as `<name>` at its
start tag, and `Rendered::missingGlyphs` lists each character no font has
(`extensions/pdf/tests/layout.rs`). `Rendered::overflows` lists margin, header, footer and slot
markup taller than its area (`crates/nvs-ext/tests/pdf.rs`). What the layout does not do yet is in
the module docs of `extensions/pdf/src/layout.rs` and the files under `extensions/pdf/src/layout/`.

**Declined:**
- **A strict mode that throws on the first dropped declaration.** A test asserting `dropped` is empty
  is the strict mode, and it shows every drop at once instead of the first.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/pdf-css-subset-table`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-css-subset-table), [`core-classes/pdf-one-engine`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-one-engine), [`core-classes/spreadsheet-evaluation-and-roster`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-evaluation-and-roster).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-pdf-css-subset-table"></a>

## The CSS subset is `extensions/pdf/subset.json`, a table a test reads and the editor's data is generated from

`rule:core-classes/pdf-css-subset-table`

The CSS subset is **data**: `extensions/pdf/subset.json` lists every property, value function,
at-rule, selector and PDF-specific HTML attribute the engine implements, each with a one-line plain
description, and nothing restates it item by item. A test reads the file: every property it lists
parses, and every property it does not list is dropped and reported
([`core-classes/pdf-css-subset`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-css-subset)). The editor's completion and hover data are generated from it, so
the editor offers exactly what renders.

What the subset holds, by family — the file is the list, this is the decision:

| Family | In the subset |
|---|---|
| Cascade | type, class, id, attribute, descendant, child and sibling selectors, the structural pseudo-classes, `::before` and `::after`, specificity, inheritance, `!important`, `var()`, `calc()`, `@media print` and `all` (never `screen`), `@font-face` |
| Text | fonts and the font chain, alignment with `justify`, `line-height`, indent, decoration, transform, spacing, `white-space`, `word-break`, `overflow-wrap`, `text-overflow: ellipsis`, `vertical-align`, `font-feature-settings`, bidi, CJK line breaking, `hyphens: auto` |
| Boxes | margin, padding, borders (solid, dashed, dotted, double), `border-radius`, sizes with min and max, `box-sizing`, background colours, images and gradients, `outline`, `opacity`, `inline-block`, `display: none` |
| Lists | markers (decimal, roman, alpha, disc), `counter-reset`, `counter-increment`, `content` |
| Images | JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, SVG and a PDF page in `<img>`, inline `<svg>`, `object-fit` |
| Layout | flex and grid, floats and `clear`, `relative`, `absolute` and `fixed` positioning with `z-index`, 2D transforms |
| Pages | `@page` with size, margins, `:first`, `:left`, `:right`, `:blank` and named pages; the 16 margin boxes; `counter(page)`, `counter(pages)`, `string-set`, `string()`, `position: running()`, `element()`, `target-counter()`, `leader()`; `break-before`, `break-after`, `break-inside`, the `page-break-*` aliases, `orphans`, `widows` |
| Tables | [`core-classes/pdf-tables-across-pages`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-tables-across-pages), with `box-decoration-break: slice` |
| HTML | `data-repeat`, `data-mark`, `<slot name>`, `<a href>` to `http(s):`, `mailto:` and `#anchor`, `<title>`, `<meta>`, `lang` |

**Out of the subset, dropped and reported:** footnotes, multi-column, `box-shadow`, `text-shadow`,
`filter`, masks, `clip-path`, blend modes, 3D transforms, animation, transitions, `position: sticky`,
vertical writing modes, ruby, subgrid, `box-decoration-break: clone`, form fields, `<iframe>`,
`<video>` and `<canvas>`. `<script>` never runs. Splitting one flex line or grid row across pages is
out too: a row moves to the next page whole.

The line between in and out is one test: **every common case is in, an edge case is in when it is
easy, and a hard edge case almost nobody needs in a document stays out.** Everything on the out list
either draws nothing on paper (animation, transitions, `sticky`), needs a second layout model for a
rare document (footnotes, multi-column, vertical writing, ruby, subgrid) or is a raster effect a
vector file draws badly (shadows, filters, masks, blend modes).

- **Memory:** none at run time beyond the cascade's computed styles, which are part of the layout tree.

**The editor carries only what its own data lacks**, the entries `subset.json` marks `"editor":
true`: `data-repeat` with its four values and `data-mark` as global HTML attributes, shown in every
HTML region because the editor cannot know which markup becomes a PDF, and `string-set` with the 16
margin-box at-rules. VS Code's CSS service keeps its own entry for a name another provider repeats,
and its HTML service lists a repeated tag twice and hovers only its own, so a second `content` or
`<slot>` would change nothing. The value functions `running()`, `element()`, `string()`,
`target-counter()` and `leader()` are carried by neither file: the custom-data format has no place
for a function, and VS Code's CSS linter does not mark an unknown one.

**On disk.** `extensions/pdf/subset.json` is the list, and `extensions/pdf/tests/css.rs` holds it
equal to the properties `extensions/pdf/src/css/properties.rs` parses.
`editors/vscode/scripts/customData.ts` makes the editor's two files from it, `bun nv
pdf-custom-data` writes them under `editors/vscode/data/`, `editors/vscode/package.json` contributes
them, and the contributions suite fails when either differs from what the generator makes. Every
hover links the `Novis\Pdf\Document` reference page.

**Declined:**
- **The subset as prose only.** A list nothing reads drifts from what the engine parses, and the
  editor could not complete from it.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/pdf-css-subset`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-css-subset), [`core-classes/pdf-tables-across-pages`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-tables-across-pages), [`ide/a-template-region-gets-the-editors-services-and-formatter`](ide.md#ide-a-template-region-gets-the-editors-services-and-formatter).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-pdf-tables-across-pages"></a>

## A table across pages keeps its columns, repeats its header and footer, never cuts a line and closes its borders

`rule:core-classes/pdf-tables-across-pages`

A table that runs over several pages follows **eight rules, each a default with no configuration**:

1. **Column widths are computed once for the whole table**, so every page has the same columns.
2. **`thead` repeats at the top and `tfoot` at the bottom of every page the table is on.** A row
   inside either says when it shows with `data-repeat`: `every` (the default), `first`, `last`, or
   `continued`, which shows only where the table goes on to another page.
3. **A row that fits on a page is never split.** A row taller than a page splits between lines of
   text, never through a line, an image or a glyph, and each cell continues on the next page.
4. **Borders are closed at every break**: the table's outer border and collapsed cell borders are
   drawn on both sides of it. `box-decoration-break: slice` on the table restores CSS's open edge.
5. **A header is never alone.** `orphans` and `widows` on a table count rows, default 2, and a table
   never starts at a page bottom with only its `thead`.
6. **A `<tbody>` and a `rowspan` group stay together** when they fit on a page, and split between
   rows when they do not.
7. **The caption shows on the first page only**, and `:nth-child` striping follows source order.
8. **A `<slot name="…">` in a repeated row** is filled per page by `Document::slots`
   ([`core-classes/pdf-header-is-a-page-function`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-header-is-a-page-function)). The slot keeps its row's height, so filling it
   never moves anything, and text that does not fit is listed in `Rendered::overflows`.

They are the rules an invoice, a statement and a long report need, and browsers keep only the second
half of the second: a table cut through a line of text, a lone header at a page bottom, an open border
and a carried-forward total that cannot be written are each a reason a program reaches for a second
tool. Each rule is the reading a person expects, so none needs a setting.

- **Memory:** the table's column widths and each row's height, once, as part of the layout tree,
  and each slot's box once on each page its row is drawn on.

**On disk.** `extensions/pdf/src/layout/table.rs` lays a table out by the eight rules, and its
module doc names what it does not do yet. A closed edge takes its border and padding from each
page it is drawn on.

**Declined:**
- **A setting per rule.** Each default is the one a document wants; `data-repeat`,
  `box-decoration-break` and `orphans` already override where a document wants otherwise.
- **Running totals in the table engine.** `data-mark` and a slot write one, with the arithmetic in
  Novis.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/pdf-header-is-a-page-function`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-header-is-a-page-function), [`core-classes/pdf-css-subset-table`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-css-subset-table).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-pdf-header-is-a-page-function"></a>

## A header, a footer or a slot is a Novis function called once per page, placed by a second call that never moves the body

`rule:core-classes/pdf-header-is-a-page-function`

A header, a footer or a table slot that needs the program's own logic is a **Novis function called once
per page** with that page's `Page`, returning ``html`…` `` markup. Headers that need no logic are CSS:
the 16 margin boxes, `counter(page)`, `counter(pages)`, `string-set` and running elements, all in the
subset ([`core-classes/pdf-css-subset-table`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-css-subset-table)).

**A render with a function is two calls to the component.** The first, `render-first`, lays out the
body and returns it as a `kept` resource the request holds
([`packaging/a-fresh-instance-per-request`](packaging.md#packaging-a-fresh-instance-per-request)), beside each page's facts with no file. Novis then calls
each function once per page, with no crossing. The second, `render-second`, takes that resource and every
page's markup, places the markup in the margins and slots of the kept pages, and writes the file. Each
render has its own resource, so a function that renders another document, with functions of its own,
leaves the outer render's body as it was. A resource is written once, and a second `render-second` with
it returns `invalid`.

**A header never moves the body.** Each margin's height is fixed before the body is laid out, by
`@page`'s margin or the function's `height` option, so the page breaks the function saw are the page
breaks of the file. Markup taller than its margin is clipped to it and listed in `Rendered::overflows`
with its page: markup that goes on to a second page of its area, and a run of text or an image that
reaches below the area's bottom on its one page. A slot keeps its row's height, so filling it moves
nothing either, and its fill's `body` has no margin unless the fill's own `<style>` gives it one, so
the fill starts at its content box's top-left corner. Where a margin box and
a function both fill one margin, the function's markup is drawn.

**`Page`** carries the number, the count, whether it is the first or the last, its named page, its
`string-set` values and its **marks**. A mark is `data-mark="name:value"` on any element, several
separated by `;`. `marks(name)` returns the values on that page and `marksUpTo(name)` those on every
page up to it, as strings, so a carried-forward total is `Core\Decimal` arithmetic in Novis and never
rounds through a float.

- **Memory:** between the two calls, the request keeps one laid-out body per unfinished render, inside
  the request's cap. `render-second` frees it, and the request's end frees one left behind. Novis holds one `Page` per page and the markup the
  functions return.

**On disk.** The CSS half is `extensions/pdf/src/layout/margin.rs`, and the two passes are
`first` and `second` in `extensions/pdf/src/lib.rs`, with the guest's `Body` as the resource, called by `Document::render` in
`extensions/pdf/nvs/Document.nvs`. A function's `height` is an `@page` rule after the document's
own, so a `:first`, `:left`, `:right`, `:blank` or named-page rule's margin on that side still wins
over it. `Document::slots` fills each `<slot name>` through the same second pass, in its cell's
content box.

**Declined:**
- **A function called from the guest per page.** The world has no export a guest calls back into
  Novis through, and a crossing per page costs more than one batch.
- **Laying the body out again with the headers in place.** A header that moved the body would change
  the page breaks the function saw, and the page count with them.
- **Running totals computed by the engine.** Which marks add up, in which currency and rounding, is
  the program's; the engine reports where each mark landed.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/pdf-roster`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-roster), [`core-classes/pdf-tables-across-pages`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-tables-across-pages), [`packaging/a-fresh-instance-per-request`](packaging.md#packaging-a-fresh-instance-per-request), [`core-classes/html-template`](core-classes.md#core-classes-html-template).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-pdf-output-is-inert"></a>

## The writer emits nothing a reader would execute, the invoice XML is its one attachment, and equal input gives byte-equal output

`rule:core-classes/pdf-output-is-inert`

The writer never emits JavaScript, launch actions, an open action, form fields, or any construct that
makes a reader fetch or execute on open. Links exist only where the source wrote one with an `http(s):`,
`mailto:` or `#anchor` target. Rendering `tainted` input is safe by construction — the render is a
transform, not a sink — and a program embedding untrusted markup that wants its *tags* constrained
sanitizes first ([`core-classes/html-sanitize`](core-classes.md#core-classes-html-sanitize)).

The one embedded file the writer ever emits is a **Factur-X invoice XML**, under PDF/A-3b only
([`core-classes/pdf-factur-x-is-the-one-attachment`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-factur-x-is-the-one-attachment)). An embedded file a reader opens is a
delivery channel for anything, so no other attachment exists, and the invoice XML is data the reader
parses, never opens.

The writer embeds **no timestamp unless the program passes one, and no generator entropy**: the
document id is derived from the content, and nothing depends on hash-map order or on float formatting
that varies between runs. So two renders of equal input are byte-equal, including encrypted output,
whose salts and key are derived the same way ([`core-classes/pdf-standards-and-passwords`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-standards-and-passwords)). That
turns a document test into a byte comparison and removes the class of flaky fixture every PDF test
suite otherwise grows.

The component's fixtures owe a scanner over the output of the whole fixture corpus that finds no
`/JavaScript`, `/Launch` or `/OpenAction` object and no `/EmbeddedFile` outside the Factur-X fixtures,
and the same input rendered twice and compared byte for byte, encrypted output among it.

**On disk.** `extensions/pdf/src/write.rs` writes through `krilla` with no creation time
unless one is passed, and `krilla`'s document id hashes the content. Each link is a URI or an
internal annotation the source wrote. `crates/nvs-ext/tests/pdf.rs` compares two renders byte for
byte and scans the output for the names above, and `crates/nvs-ext/tests/pdf_standards.rs` holds the
Factur-X file to its one attachment and two encrypted renders to byte equality.

**Declined:**
- **Any attachment besides the invoice XML.** A program that needs to send several files sends them
  beside the PDF.
- **A creation time read from a clock.** The guest has none, and a time the program did not ask for
  breaks byte equality.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/pdf-render-has-no-io`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-render-has-no-io), [`core-classes/html-sanitize`](core-classes.md#core-classes-html-sanitize), [`core-classes/pdf-factur-x-is-the-one-attachment`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-factur-x-is-the-one-attachment), [`core-classes/spreadsheet-output-is-inert`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-output-is-inert), [`core-classes/pdf-page-is-an-image-source`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-page-is-an-image-source).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-pdf-standards-and-passwords"></a>

## Every PDF is tagged, a chosen PDF/A or PDF/UA standard is validated, and a password encrypts with AES-256 alone

`rule:core-classes/pdf-standards-and-passwords`

**Every render is a tagged PDF**: headings, paragraphs, lists, tables with their header cells, figures
with their `alt` text and the document's language come from the HTML, with no option to turn it off.
`Document::standard` adds one of **PDF/A-2b, PDF/A-3b or PDF/UA-1**, and a document that breaks the
standard it chose throws `LogicError` naming what broke — an image with no `alt` under PDF/UA-1, a
font that cannot be embedded under PDF/A — through `krilla`'s own validation. One standard per
document, because `krilla` validates against one. PDF/A needs `Document::created`, because the
component reads no clock, and PDF/UA-1 needs a `<title>`. A missing glyph, reported and never thrown
otherwise, throws under any of the three, because each forbids the empty box drawn for it.

**`Document::password`** encrypts with **AES-256, revision 6**, and nothing weaker. Its salts and its
file key are derived from a hash of the document and the password, so equal input stays byte-equal
([`core-classes/pdf-output-is-inert`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-output-is-inert)). A password beside a PDF/A standard throws `LogicError`,
because PDF/A forbids encryption.

Tagging costs a structure tree the size of the element tree and buys a document a screen reader can
read; it is the default because a program that never thought about accessibility should still produce
an accessible file. AES-256 alone is offered because every reader made in the last fifteen years opens
it and the weaker revisions are broken.

- **Memory:** the structure tree, beside the layout tree inside the request's cap, and with a
  password one more copy of the finished file while it is encrypted.
- **Performance:** a password adds four runs of the standard's password hash, each 64 or more rounds
