  of AES and SHA-2, and one AES pass over the file.

**On disk.** `Document::standard` and `Document::password` are in
`extensions/pdf/nvs/Document.nvs`, and a password beside a PDF/A standard is refused before anything
is laid out (`extensions/pdf/src/lib.rs`'s `first`). Tagging and the three standards are
`extensions/pdf/src/write.rs`, and the encryption is `extensions/pdf/src/encrypt.rs`, over the file
`krilla` writes because `krilla` 0.8 writes no encryption. The password is both the user and the owner
password. All of it is pinned by `crates/nvs-ext/tests/pdf_standards.rs`, which opens the encrypted
file with `hayro-syntax`.

**Declined:**
- **RC4 and AES-128 encryption, and owner permissions.** RC4 is broken, and permission flags are a
  request to the reader that any tool ignores.
- **Form filling and signatures.** Each is a second model of the file: fields the reader edits, and a
  signing key and timestamp authority the program must own. A program that signs uses a signing
  service.
- **Untagged output.** It saves a few percent of the file and gives up the document's accessibility.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/pdf-output-is-inert`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-output-is-inert), [`core-classes/pdf-factur-x-is-the-one-attachment`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-factur-x-is-the-one-attachment).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-pdf-factur-x-is-the-one-attachment"></a>

## A Factur-X XML under PDF/A-3b is the one attachment a rendered PDF carries

`rule:core-classes/pdf-factur-x-is-the-one-attachment`

`Document::invoiceXml` embeds **exactly one Factur-X (ZUGFeRD) XML file**, under PDF/A-3b only, and it
is the only attachment the writer ever emits ([`core-classes/pdf-output-is-inert`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-output-is-inert)). The file name,
the `AFRelationship` and the XMP fields are the ones the standard fixes, so the program passes the XML
and nothing else. The XML is checked well-formed, inside the request's memory cap and with no entity
expansion, and is otherwise the program's to build. The component reads one thing from it: the
guideline id of its `GuidelineSpecifiedDocumentContextParameter`, which gives the profile
`fx:ConformanceLevel` names, `EN 16931` when the id is not one the standard lists. `MINIMUM` and
`BASIC WL` are attached as `Data`, because neither is a whole invoice, and every other profile as
`Alternative`.

An invoice XML without `Document::Standard::PdfA3b` throws `LogicError`, because Factur-X is defined
only on PDF/A-3. An XML that is not well-formed throws `ParseError`, and so does one that nests
elements more than 256 levels deep. A real invoice nests about ten, and the bound keeps a hostile one
from costing more than its node tree. `Reader::invoiceXml` returns the XML of a received invoice
([`core-classes/pdf-reader-and-merge`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-reader-and-merge)), and throws `ParseError` for one that parses and nests
deeper than 256 levels.

An e-invoice is the one attachment businesses are required to send, and a hybrid PDF is how most of
Europe sends it. Any other attachment is a file a reader may be asked to open, which is the
delivery channel `pdf-output-is-inert` closes.

- **Memory:** the XML once, inside the request's cap, and the bytes it adds to the output.

**On disk.** `Document::invoiceXml` is in `extensions/pdf/nvs/Document.nvs`. An invoice XML without
PDF/A-3b, and one that is not well-formed, is refused before anything is laid out
(`extensions/pdf/src/lib.rs`'s `first`). `extensions/pdf/src/factur_x.rs` checks, embeds and writes
the XMP fields, and its module doc says how.

**Declined:**
- **General attachments.** A file a reader opens from inside a PDF is a delivery channel for anything,
  and a program sends other files beside the PDF.
- **Building or validating the invoice's content.** The XML schema and the invoice's rules belong to
  the program's invoicing code, which already knows the invoice.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/pdf-output-is-inert`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-output-is-inert), [`core-classes/pdf-standards-and-passwords`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-standards-and-passwords), [`core-classes/pdf-reader-and-merge`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-reader-and-merge).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-pdf-reader-and-merge"></a>

## Existing PDFs are placed, merged and read in `Novis\Pdf`, and an encrypted source throws

`rule:core-classes/pdf-reader-and-merge`

Existing PDFs are **placed, merged and read in `Novis\Pdf`**; only rasterising a page is the image
component's ([`core-classes/pdf-page-is-an-image-source`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-page-is-an-image-source)).

- **Placing.** `<img src="terms.pdf#page=2">` draws that page of an asset as vector content, and
  `@page { background-image: url(letterhead.pdf) }` draws it behind every page. Only the page's
  appearance is kept: its links, form fields and bookmarks are not.
- **Merging.** `Pages::merge` takes PDFs, each with an optional list of page numbers, and returns one
  PDF. Merging, splitting, reordering and removing pages are that one call: a list that repeats a
  page repeats it, and a list that leaves one out removes it.
- **Reading.** `Reader::open` returns the page count, the metadata (title, author, subject, keywords,
  creator, producer), the attachments by name, and `invoiceXml()`, the Factur-X XML of a received
  invoice or `null`. `text($page)` returns a page's text in the order the file stores it, through
  `hayro`'s interpreter and each font's Unicode map. It does not rebuild tables or columns.

**An encrypted source throws `ParseError`** in all three, as the image side does
([`core-classes/pdf-decode-refusals`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-decode-refusals)), and so does a source that does not parse. A page number
outside its document throws `LogicError` naming the page count. **A stream that decompresses past
[`core-classes/decompression-bound`](core-classes.md#core-classes-decompression-bound) throws `ParseError`** in all three, naming the half of the
bound that stopped it and the `[limits]` key that raises it. Each job is one call: `Reader::open`
reads the count, the metadata and the attachments together, and `text` takes the bytes again with only
the pages it asks for.

These are the jobs a program does with the PDFs it receives and sends — attach the terms, put a
letterhead under a letter, read back an uploaded invoice — and each was a reason to install a second
tool. They live beside the writer because they return text and bytes, never pixels.

- **Memory:** per call, the source bytes and what the call returns, inside the request's cap; a merge
  holds its sources and the merged file at once.

**On disk.** The component places, merges and reads (`extensions/pdf/src/read.rs`,
`extensions/pdf/src/merge.rs`, `extensions/pdf/src/layout/image.rs`), pinned by
`crates/nvs-ext/tests/pdf_read.rs`, and `extensions/pdf/nvs/Pages.nvs` and `Reader.nvs` are the
classes a program calls, pinned by `tests/conformance/novis/pdf-merge-takes-chosen-pages.nvst` and
`pdf-reader-returns-an-invoice-xml-and-text.nvst`. A written page list such as `[3, 1]` crosses
because the crossing takes a non-negative `int` as a `uint` (`crates/nvs-ext/src/convert.rs`).

**Declined:**
- **Rebuilding tables and columns from extracted text.** That is a layout guess, right for some files
  and wrong for others; the file's own order is the honest answer.
- **Decrypting a source with a password.** A received encrypted PDF is opened by the person it was
  sent to, and the password is theirs.
- **Editing a page's content in place.** It is a second, imperative model of the file
  ([`core-classes/pdf-one-engine`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-one-engine)); a new page is HTML.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/pdf-page-is-an-image-source`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-page-is-an-image-source), [`core-classes/pdf-decode-refusals`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-decode-refusals), [`core-classes/pdf-factur-x-is-the-one-attachment`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-factur-x-is-the-one-attachment).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-pdf-default-fonts"></a>

## The Liberation fonts render a document with no font of its own, and a missing glyph is reported, never thrown

`rule:core-classes/pdf-default-fonts`

The PDF component carries **Liberation Sans, Serif and Mono in regular, bold, italic and bold
italic**, so a plain document renders with no font in its asset map. `sans-serif`, Arial and Helvetica
map to Sans, `serif`, Times and Times New Roman to Serif, and `monospace` and Courier to Mono. The same
twelve files stand in for the standard-14 fonts when the image component rasterises a PDF
([`core-classes/pdf-page-is-an-image-source`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-page-is-an-image-source)), and live once in the tree under `extensions/fonts/`.

**The font chain** of a run of text is the `@font-face` fonts its `font-family` names, from the asset
map, then the default of its generic family. A character no font in the chain has is drawn as the
font's empty box and listed in `Rendered::missingGlyphs` with the chain it tried. It never throws: the
rest of the document is right, and a program that must have every glyph asserts the list is empty. A
font file that does not parse throws `ParseError` naming it. Every font is subset into the output, so
a document carries only the glyphs it draws.

There is no system font lookup, because the guest has no filesystem, and a render on a laptop and on a
server gives the same bytes.

The Liberation fonts are under **OFL-1.1**, admitted for font data only: the binary's attribution
carries their licence and copyright ([`packaging/the-third-party-notice-is-generated-never-written-by-hand`](packaging.md#packaging-the-third-party-notice-is-generated-never-written-by-hand)),
and no code under OFL-1.1 is admitted by it.

- **Memory:** the twelve fonts are part of each component's bytes, a few megabytes of the binary. A
  render holds the faces it uses inside its request's cap.

The twelve files are under `extensions/fonts/` with their release recorded in `SOURCE.json`, and the
image and PDF components embed them. `extensions/pdf/src/fonts.rs` maps the family names above to
them, registers each `@font-face` font from the asset map, and builds the chain;
`extensions/pdf/src/layout.rs` lists the missing glyphs, and `extensions/pdf/tests/layout.rs` holds
the chain, the subsetting and the missing-glyph list.

**Declined:**
- **Noto or another font with wide script coverage as a default.** Its size grows the binary by tens of
  megabytes for scripts most documents never use; a document in another script passes its font as an
  asset.
- **Throwing on a missing glyph.** One unknown character in a customer's name would lose the whole
  invoice.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/pdf-css-subset`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-css-subset), [`core-classes/pdf-page-is-an-image-source`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-page-is-an-image-source), [`packaging/the-third-party-notice-is-generated-never-written-by-hand`](packaging.md#packaging-the-third-party-notice-is-generated-never-written-by-hand).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-pdf-page-is-an-image-source"></a>

## A PDF page is a decode-only format of the image component: one page per `open`, priced by the pixel cap

`rule:core-classes/pdf-page-is-an-image-source`

Rasterising a PDF page is a **decode-only format of the image component**, not a member of
`Novis\Pdf`: a raster produced there would have to recross the boundary to enter the pipeline that is
the whole point of loading one. Reading a PDF's text, metadata and attachments, and merging pages, are
`Novis\Pdf`'s ([`core-classes/pdf-reader-and-merge`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-reader-and-merge)), because they return text and bytes rather
than pixels. No new entry point is added;
the format enum simply gains a case.

`open` gains two options meaningful for a paged source: a 1-based **page**, default `1`, and a
**dpi**, default `150`. One call rasterises exactly that page, so a document's pages become images by
iterating and cost stays proportional to what was asked for. The pixel price is the page box scaled
to the requested resolution, `ceil(width_pt × dpi / 72) × ceil(height_pt × dpi / 72)`, counted
against the pixel cap before any buffer is allocated ([`core-classes/image-pixel-cap`](core-classes.md#core-classes-image-pixel-cap)), so the
same bytes refused at one dpi pass at a lower one. A page beyond the document throws a `RuntimeError`
naming the page count.

`info` parses the cross-reference table and page tree and never a content stream: `format` is
`Format::Pdf`, `frames` is the **page count**, and `width` and `height` are the first page's box in
whole points. Counting pages is one header-only call that allocates no pixel.

Rasterising is a pure function of the bytes and the options — no clock, no I/O, no system fonts — so
equal input gives byte-equal output. The interpreter is **hayro**, pure Rust, compiled into the
sandbox beside the codecs, with the Liberation fonts ([`core-classes/pdf-default-fonts`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-default-fonts)) standing
in for the standard-14 fonts so an unembedded-font document renders. It is linked only once it builds
for the component's `wasm32` target and its dependency tree passes `cargo deny` over the component's
own graph. There is no fallback interpreter. The sandbox is where a parser this large
belongs: the hostile-bytes surface it leaves is contained by the sandbox's memory cap and epoch
deadline like every other decoder's, and the build gains no C.

The decoder's fixtures owe, asserted inside the guest: a 100-page document whose `info` gives
`frames: 100` and `Format::Pdf` with no pixel buffer allocated and one host-to-guest call; a page box
over the cap at one `dpi` that passes at a lower one; `{page: 7}` of a three-page document throwing
with the count 3; the same page rasterised twice byte-equal; and a benchmark of one text page and one
image-heavy page, guest against the same crate native.

- **Memory:** a request that opens a PDF holds the encoded document and one page's raster of at most
  the pixel cap, 96 MiB at the default cap in RGBA8, inside the extension's existing store limits, and
  nothing outlives the request. The interpreter and the font substitutes grow the binary by
  single-digit megabytes. CPU is the request's epoch deadline, and bulk rasterising is queue work.

A page is drawn on white, so every pixel is opaque, and a side may be at most 65535 pixels, which is
`hayro`'s renderer's own bound. Symbol and ZapfDingbats are drawn in Liberation Serif and Sans, which
have few of their glyphs. No predefined CMap is carried, so CJK text in an encoding that names one is
not drawn; carrying them is `hayro`'s `embed-cmaps` feature. The decoder is
`extensions/image/src/pdf.rs`, and its fixtures are `crates/nvs-ext/tests/image_decode.rs`.

The benchmark is two jobs of `crates/nvs-ext/benches/image_guest.rs`: an A4 page of text in two
unembedded standard fonts, and an A4 page drawing an 800x600 JPEG six times, each rasterised at
150 dpi. Its figures are in `benches/results/image-guest.json`. Measured on x86_64 Windows, with only
the 16-byte size crossing back, the text page is 13 ms in the guest against 9 ms native, and the
image page 53 ms against 31 ms. Returning the page's raw RGBA8 adds about 390 ms to either, because
a `list<u8>` crosses as one value per byte ([`packaging/a-guest-runs-under-the-requests-budget`](packaging.md#packaging-a-guest-runs-under-the-requests-budget)).
The text page's pixels agree with native to within one level per channel, at the anti-aliased
edges of its glyphs, and the image page's byte for byte (`crates/nvs-ext/tests/image_guest.rs`).

**Declined:**
- **A `rasterize` member in `Novis\Pdf`.** Every raster would recross the boundary as bytes to reach
  `resize`.
- **pdfium or MuPDF compiled to wasm, as the interpreter or as a fallback.** pdfium in wasm needs
  Emscripten and has no WASI build, and MuPDF is AGPL and outside `deny.toml`, while a pure-Rust
  interpreter exists.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/image-pixel-cap`](core-classes.md#core-classes-image-pixel-cap), [`core-classes/image-format-roster`](core-classes.md#core-classes-image-format-roster), [`core-classes/pdf-decode-refusals`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-decode-refusals), [`core-classes/pdf-default-fonts`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-default-fonts).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-pdf-decode-refusals"></a>

## An encrypted document and a detectable omission both throw, and reading and merging are `Novis\Pdf`'s

`rule:core-classes/pdf-decode-refusals`

An **encrypted document throws** a `ParseError` naming the encryption. There is no password option,
and decrypting stays in the third-party channel. An **embedded object the engine recognises but cannot
decode throws** naming the object, rather than rendering a blank region: a generated image must be
deterministic, not approximately right, and a silently incomplete raster is a repair
([`errors/ambiguous-input-refused`](errors.md#errors-ambiguous-input-refused)). An external reference never resolves, because nothing in the
guest can resolve one, and JavaScript, launch actions and embedded files are inert by construction,
since rasterising reads a page's appearance and never executes an action.

Text extraction, metadata, attachments, and splitting and merging pages are **different jobs over the
same bytes**, and are `Novis\Pdf`'s ([`core-classes/pdf-reader-and-merge`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-reader-and-merge)), which refuses an
encrypted source the same way. Form filling, signing and password decryption are no component's, and
belong to the third-party channel. A document the interpreter renders wrong has no first-party
fallback.

The surface this leaves open is an *approximated* construct — one the interpreter supports but
renders imperfectly — which is a silent fidelity miss rather than a detectable omission, and is owned
as a known consequence rather than closed by a rule.

The decoder's fixtures hold this inside the guest, and owe:
- an encrypted fixture that throws `ParseError` naming the encryption, and a fixture embedding an
  object the engine cannot decode that throws naming it;
- a fixture carrying an external reference, a JavaScript action and an embedded file that rasterises
  with nothing resolved, nothing executed and no network or filesystem access observable;
- a **bomb corpus** — recursive form XObjects, an xref loop, a stream-length lie and a deflate bomb —
  where each case ends in a throw, a contained trap under the request's limits, or its page drawn
  whole as a reader that is not fooled draws it, never a hang. `hayro` repairs a broken
  cross-reference table and a lying stream length, and cuts a form that draws itself, so those three
  are drawn; refusing them would refuse every real file with a damaged table.

An encrypted document is opened with a password nobody sets, so one whose user password is empty is
refused too. A font in an encoding `hayro` cannot draw, and an image that does not decode, throw
`RuntimeError` naming the page.

**On disk.** `extensions/image/src/pdf.rs` throws `ParseError` for an encrypted document and
`RuntimeError` for an image that does not decode, a page carrying a link, a JavaScript and a launch
action and an embedded file is drawn from its content alone, and the bomb corpus ends in a throw, a
contained trap or a whole page (`crates/nvs-ext/tests/image_decode.rs`). The throw for a font
`hayro` cannot draw has no fixture yet.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/pdf-page-is-an-image-source`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-page-is-an-image-source), [`core-classes/pdf-reader-and-merge`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-reader-and-merge), [`errors/ambiguous-input-refused`](errors.md#errors-ambiguous-input-refused).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-spreadsheet-has-no-io"></a>

## `Novis\Spreadsheet` is a built-in component that never touches disk, fetches nothing and executes nothing it reads

`rule:core-classes/spreadsheet-has-no-io`

`Novis\Spreadsheet` is the fourth component built into every `nvs` binary
([`packaging/the-first-party-components-are-built-in`](packaging.md#packaging-the-first-party-components-are-built-in)), sandboxed, always present under
`Novis\`, with `Novis\Spreadsheet\Engine` as its manifest class and every other class Novis source
that calls it ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-roster`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-roster)). It is not `Core`: a spreadsheet API is a
permanent simplicity cost, and its parsers unsandboxed in every in-flight request is the outcome the
tier system exists to prevent. It is not Native either, because nothing in it holds connection state
or privilege, and the sandbox is the feature. It is not an `[[extension]]` package, because an
export and an import of an upload are jobs nearly every web application has, and a program could not
know whether the package exists without asking its deployment.

The placement holds because an uploaded workbook is the tier's exact hostile-bytes material: xlsx is a
zip of XML, where external entities and decompression bombs are the genre's vulnerability history, and
legacy xls is an OLE compound binary. One guest call per batch of rows or per read-ahead block makes
the boundary crossing noise beside the work ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-bulk-boundary`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-bulk-boundary)).

**The component never touches disk, and is granted nothing.** Writing returns compressed chunks, and
the Novis half sends them on to the response, the file or the memory the program chose
([`core-classes/spreadsheet-writes-as-a-stream`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-writes-as-a-stream)). Reading pulls byte ranges of a `Core\IO\File`
the program opened, or of `bytes` it holds, through the call that lent them
([`core-classes/spreadsheet-reads-as-a-stream`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-reads-as-a-stream)). No preopen and no outbound HTTP is granted to the
component, under any configuration. **The component fetches nothing**: an external-workbook reference,
a linked image or a data connection in a read file comes back as **data** — the reference itself — and
is never resolved, and an image placed on write is bytes the caller supplies.

**CSV goes through the same classes and is parsed and formatted by `Core\Csv` in the Novis half**, so
CSV has one parser and one API for the job. **A workbook reads as a workbook**: a source that starts
with a zip's `PK` and a control byte, or with a compound file's `D0 CF 11 E0`, goes to the engine
whatever the options say. `Reader::open`'s second argument is `{csv?: {separator?, quote?, escape?,
encoding?: Core\Charset}}`, and each field means what `Core\Csv`'s or `Core\Encoding`'s option of
that name means; `Core\Csv` checks the dialect once at `open`, so a wrong one throws there. The
options are a `csv` field so that a reader of the call knows they apply to CSV alone. **The charset
is the program's or the byte order mark's, and nothing guesses it.** With an `encoding` other than
UTF-8, or with no `encoding` and a UTF-16 byte order mark, the source is decoded whole with
`Core\Encoding::decodeText`, its mark dropped, and parsed with `Core\Csv::parse`; a file is read
whole first through the engine's `sourceBytes`, because `Core\IO\File` reads text only, and keeps
its position. A byte that is not text in that charset throws `decodeText`'s `RuntimeError`.
Otherwise a source is CSV when its start is UTF-8 (`bytes` decoded whole, a file's first four
bytes, walked with `Core\Csv::rows`), and anything else goes to the engine, which throws for a file
that is no workbook. A CSV is one sheet, `Sheet1`, with no extras. `rows` takes every option and gives the xlsx row shape:
the header keys numbered and lettered as the engine does, an empty field an empty cell, a short
record's missing keys `null`, a record numbered by its place in the file. Every value is a `string`.
`Workbook` writes CSV for a name ending in `.csv` or `{format: 'csv'}`: each batch of rows goes
through `Core\Csv::format` with each value as its text, and a second sheet throws naming both.
`Workbook`'s options and `fromRows`'s take `csv?: {separator?, quote?, encoding?: Core\Charset}`,
checked by `Core\Csv` at create. With an `encoding` other than UTF-8, each batch's text is encoded
with `Core\Encoding::encodeText`, a UTF-16 file starts with a byte order mark so that it reads back
with no option, and a download's `Content-Type` names no charset. **A character the charset lacks
throws `LogicError` naming its cell**, such as `B3`, counted from the file's first row: the batch is
encoded whole, and only when that throws is each field encoded alone to find the cell. The
engine still opens a writer, which checks the sheet name and logs a workbook never finished, and its
bytes are dropped, so styles, widths and every sheet-end part are left out. **A string that starts
with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage return is written with a `'` first**, because Excel reads
such a field as a formula, and a string is always text; reading does not strip it.

- **Performance:** a CSV write still instantiates the component once, for the writer's checks; the
  rows never cross. A read of `bytes` parses the whole text each time `sheets` or `rows` walks it.
- **Memory:** a read of `bytes` holds the decoded text and its records, per request; a read of a
  `Core\IO\File` holds one record (`Core\Csv::rows`). A write holds one batch of rows.
- **Usability:** one import loop for xlsx and CSV. The `'` a guarded string carries is in the file
  for every tool that reads it, not only for Excel.

**Reading evaluates nothing.** A cell reads as its stored scalar, or as its formula text with the cached
result the file's author wrote beside it, and the two are distinguishable at the API, because a cached
value is a claim by the author rather than a computation by us
([`core-classes/spreadsheet-value-types`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-value-types)). VBA and embedded OLE objects are inert payload the reader
may list but never executes. The XML parser resolves no entity and loads no DTD.

**Everything read is `tainted`.** `Reader::open` takes `tainted bytes`, so an upload reads, and the
source is held `tainted` whatever the program passed, because a workbook is outside data even when
the program holds it as plain `bytes`. Every string and `bytes` value `Reader` returns is `tainted`:
cells, header keys, sheet names, macro names, merged ranges and every extra. A `Formula` read with
`formulas: true` carries its text as a `tainted string`, so `Formula::text` is `tainted` for every
formula. The writer launders it with `Core\Taint::assertTrusted` at the one place a `Formula` becomes
a formula, because passing a `Formula` is the program's own choice to write one, and a string is
always text. Cost: a program that reads `->text` of a formula it made must assert it trusted too.
The engine's own results are plain shapes, because an extension call's contagion does not reach a
shape's fields (`crates/nvs-types/src/expr/quals.rs`'s `tainted_result`), so the `tainted` types are
written in `Reader`'s declarations, and a sheet name goes back to the engine through one
`assertTrusted` naming why.

The component's tests owe, asserted inside the guest: a read and a write with no capability grant that
succeed with no network or filesystem access observable; and an xlsx whose sheet XML declares an
external entity, and one carrying an external-workbook reference, each read with the reference
surfaced as data and nothing resolved.

- **Memory:** nothing until a program first uses `Novis\Spreadsheet`. Then the compiled module, held
  once per process and shared by every core, and per calling request one instance under the request's
  cap, freed when the request ends. What a write and a read hold inside it are their own fragments'.
  A CSV read in another charset holds the source's bytes, its decoded text and, for each walk, its
  records, per request; a UTF-8 file is still walked a record at a time. A CSV write in another
  charset holds one batch's text and its encoded bytes.
- **Latency:** none on a UTF-8 CSV. Another charset costs one decode of the whole source at `open`,
  or one encode per batch; a file's head is one guest call at `open`.

**Declined:**
- **A first-party `[[extension]]` package, `nvs/spreadsheet`.** It is one configuration step for a
  feature every web application uses, and `Novis\` is reserved for what the binary carries.
- **A preopen for the component, so it writes the file itself.** That is a grant of a directory to a
  parser of hostile bytes, and the Novis half already holds the file the program opened.
- **CSV left to `Core\Csv` alone, beside the component.** An import that accepts xlsx and CSV would be
  two APIs with two row shapes; through one `Reader` it is one loop.
- **A CSV string written as it is.** A string such as `=HYPERLINK(...)` from a user would run as a
  formula in Excel, and the program wrote a string, which is always text.
- **Typed CSV values, a number read as `int`.** CSV has no types, so a guess would read `00123` as
  `123`; a program converts the `string` it expects with `as ?int`.
- **Guessing a CSV's charset or separator.** Every Windows-1252 text is also valid Latin-1 and
  Windows-1250 text, so a guess turns `€` into another character in silence; the program knows where
  its files come from and names the charset.
- **A `Core\IO\File` member that reads `bytes`, for a CSV file in another charset.** It is new `Core`
  surface for one reader, and the engine already reads the file's ranges through the call it is lent.
- **Written in Novis.** It would reimplement OOXML and BIFF parsing that production crates already
  carry, unfuzzed and ours to maintain, and buy nothing the wasm build does not give. Novis code
  belongs in the builder.
- **A plain `Formula::text`, with the reader asserting a read formula trusted.** That launders a
  file's text into every sink, an HTML page included, to save a program one `assertTrusted` on a
  formula it made itself.
- **Exposing the crates' surfaces directly.** That is several disjoint APIs for one job inside a single
  component.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/spreadsheet-formula-is-a-value`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-formula-is-a-value), [`core-classes/spreadsheet-bulk-boundary`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-bulk-boundary), [`core-classes/pdf-render-has-no-io`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-render-has-no-io).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-spreadsheet-roster"></a>

## `Novis\Spreadsheet` is `Workbook`, `Sheet`, `Written`, `Export`, `Reader`, `Template`, `Style`, `Cell`, `Formula`, `Chart` and `CellError`, with `Engine` the manifest class

`rule:core-classes/spreadsheet-roster`

`Novis\Spreadsheet` is twelve classes and one enum at namespace scope, with `Engine` the manifest class whose static
methods are `wit/spreadsheet.wit`'s exports and which no program calls directly:

| Class | What it is | Its members |
|---|---|---|
| `Workbook` | A workbook being written to one target | `createForDownload(string $name, {…})`, `createForFile(string $path, {…})`, `createForStream(Core\IO\File $file, {…})`, `createInMemory({…})`, `fromRows(iterable $rows, {…}): Export`; `sheet(string $name, {…}): Sheet`, `define(string $name, string $reference): Workbook`, `finish(): Written` |
| `Sheet` | One sheet of a `Workbook`, written row by row | `add(array $row, {…}): Sheet`, `addAll(iterable $rows): Sheet`, `cell(string\|int $column, int $row): string`, `column(string\|int $column): string`, and the sheet-end parts `merge`, `link`, `note`, `validate`, `group`, `table`, `conditional`, `image`, `chart`, `print`, `protect` |
| `Written` | What `finish()` returns | `rows: array<int>` by sheet name, `size: int`, `bytes: ?bytes` |
| `Export` | A whole workbook from one call, written where its last call says | `download(string $name): void`, `save(string $path): Written`, `to(Core\IO\File $file): Written`, `bytes(): bytes` |
| `Reader` | A workbook or CSV being read | `open(Core\IO\File\|bytes $source, {csv?: {…}}): Reader`, `sheets(): array<{…}>`, `rows(string\|int $sheet, {…}): Iterator<Row>`, `evaluate(): array<{…}>`, and the extras `merged`, `links`, `notes`, `names`, `tables`, `images`, `properties`, `macros` |
| `Row` | One row `rows` read | `number: uint`, the row number in the file, and `values: array` by header text or column letter |
| `Template` | A designed workbook to fill | `open(Core\IO\File\|bytes $source): Template`, `set(string $address, mixed $value): Template`, `fill(array $data): Export` |
| `Style` | A set of style fields | `of({…}): Style` |
| `Cell` | One value with its own style, or rich text | `of(mixed $value, Style $style): Cell`, `rich(array<{text: string, style?: Style}> $runs): Cell` |
| `Formula` | A formula cell's text and its cached result | `of(string $text, {cached?: mixed}): Formula`, `text: string`, `cached: mixed` |
| `Chart` | One chart of the subset | `column`, `bar`, `line`, `area`, `pie`, `doughnut`, `scatter` (each `({…}): Chart`), `series(string $values, {…}): Chart`, `combine(Chart $other): Chart` |
| `Engine` | The manifest class | one static method per export |

The enum is `CellError`, the cell error values `#NULL!`, `#DIV/0!`, `#VALUE!`, `#REF!`, `#NAME?`,
`#NUM!`, `#N/A`, `#GETTING_DATA`, `#SPILL!` and `#CALC!` as the cases `Null`, `DivZero`, `Value`,
`Ref`, `Name`, `Num`, `NotAvailable`, `GettingData`, `Spill` and `Calc`. It stays at namespace scope,
because a cell value is `mixed` in every signature that carries one and no member names it
([`enums/an-enum-lives-in-the-class-that-uses-it`](enums.md#enums-an-enum-lives-in-the-class-that-uses-it)). Every other enum lives in the class that uses
it, and an enum that repeated its owner's name drops it:

| Owner | Its enums |
|---|---|
| `Style` | `Line`, `Underline`, `Align`, `Valign`, the types of a style's fields |
| `Reader` | `Visibility` and `SheetKind`, the types of a `sheets()` entry's `visibility` and `kind` |
| `Sheet` | `RuleKind`, `Operator`, `TotalFunction`, `ConditionalKind` and `Orientation`, the cases its sheet-end parts send |
| `Chart` | `Kind` and `Legend`, the types of a chart's `kind` and `legend` |

`Workbook` sends a sheet's visibility as a `Reader::Visibility`, and `Sheet` sends a style as a
`Style`'s enums and a chart as a `Chart`'s: those are sent to `Engine` alone, and no signature a
program calls names them.

**The target comes first, and the verb last.** A program that writes row by row names where the bytes
go when it creates the `Workbook`, so a download's headers leave at once; a one-call helper
(`Workbook::fromRows`, `Template::fill`) names it last, with the verb ([`core-api/one-paradigm-per-operation`](core-api.md#core-api-one-paradigm-per-operation)
holds each job to one of the two). **The last call of a write is `finish()`**, or the `Export`'s verb.
Each options shape is the home fragment's: the workbook's and the sheet's in
[`core-classes/spreadsheet-writes-as-a-stream`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-writes-as-a-stream), the columns and styles in
[`core-classes/spreadsheet-styles-and-defaults`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-styles-and-defaults), the reader's in
[`core-classes/spreadsheet-reads-as-a-stream`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-reads-as-a-stream), the template's in
[`core-classes/spreadsheet-template-fill`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-template-fill), and the formula helpers in
[`core-classes/spreadsheet-formula-is-a-value`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-formula-is-a-value). Every options bag is a shape
([`core-api/options-bag`](core-api.md#core-api-options-bag)).

**A cell address comes from a column key or a column letter.** `Sheet::cell($key, $row)` and
`Sheet::column($key)` take a key of the sheet's columns, or an upper-case letter from `A` to `XFD`.
Any other string is a key, so `'qty'` and `'a'` are keys. A key before the first keyed row throws
`LogicError` naming it, `column` before the first data row throws, and either call on a finished
sheet throws naming the sheet. The column a call reaches is checked against 16,384 before it is
narrowed, so the message names the number the program gave.

**An error throws the world's three classes.** A call the program got wrong — a bad sheet name, an
`Instant` with no zone, a row past the grid, a placeholder the data lacks — throws `LogicError`
naming the rule it broke and the cell, column or sheet. A file that does not read — a broken archive,
a lying record length, a bomb — throws `ParseError`. Anything else the component reports throws
`RuntimeError`. A trap throws `ExtensionError`, and the request's memory or CPU cap ends the request
([`packaging/a-guest-crash-throws`](packaging.md#packaging-a-guest-crash-throws)).

**A rich cell is one text cell of runs.** `Cell::rich` takes each run's `text` and an optional
`Style` that sets font fields alone: `font`, `size`, `bold`, `italic`, `strike`, `underline` and
`color`. Any other field throws `LogicError` naming the field and the run, because Excel styles a
run's font and nothing else, and an empty list throws too. The cell's fill, border, alignment and
format come from its row and its column. A rich cell has `value` `null` and its runs in the readonly
`runs`, which is `null` for every other cell. `Workbook` sends it as `cell-value::rich`, each run's
style a `writer-style` id. The reader reads it as its runs' text joined, and CSV writes that text.

**On disk.** Every member the table names, in `extensions/spreadsheet/nvs/`, and the enums in
`extensions/spreadsheet/manifest.json`, each with its `owner`. A `Style` also has the readonly
`fields` and `key` that `Workbook` reads.

**Declined:**
- **One `Spreadsheet` class with every member.** Writing, reading and filling share no state, and a
  class per job keeps each card short.
- **`createForMemory`.** `createInMemory` says where the bytes stay, the way the other three name a
  target.
- **A `CellError` owned by `Reader`.** No signature names it, so the enum rule places it in the
  namespace.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/spreadsheet-has-no-io`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-has-no-io), [`core-classes/spreadsheet-writes-as-a-stream`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-writes-as-a-stream), [`core-classes/spreadsheet-reads-as-a-stream`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-reads-as-a-stream), [`core-api/options-bag`](core-api.md#core-api-options-bag).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-spreadsheet-writes-as-a-stream"></a>

## A workbook is written as a stream to the target it was created for, one sheet after another, and finished with `finish()`

`rule:core-classes/spreadsheet-writes-as-a-stream`

A workbook is written as a stream to the target it was created for, and **streaming is the only way to
write xlsx**: a row's values and styles are final once written, and there is no in-memory editable mode.
An ods is written from the same calls, and held until `finish()` (below).

**The four targets**, each a `Workbook` static method that takes the workbook options last:

| Method | Where the bytes go |
|---|---|
| `createForDownload(string $name, {…})` | The response. It sets `Content-Disposition` with `$name` and starts `Core\Response::stream` at once, so the headers leave before the first row is written |
| `createForFile(string $path, {…})` | A file, opened with `Core\IO::open` in `Write` mode and written with `Core\IO\File::write` |
| `createForStream(Core\IO\File $file, {…})` | A file the program already opened |
| `createInMemory({…})` | Memory, and `finish()`'s `Written` carries the `bytes` |

The workbook options are `zone` (an IANA name; an `Instant` written with no `zone` throws naming its
column, [`core-classes/spreadsheet-value-types`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-value-types)), `format` (`'xlsx'`, `'ods'` or `'csv'`, defaulting
to the name's extension and then to `'xlsx'`), and `properties` (`title`, `subject`, `author`, `company`,
`keywords`, `created`). `Workbook::fromRows(iterable $rows, {…})` is the one-call form: it takes the
workbook and sheet options in one bag, writes one sheet named `sheet` (default `'Sheet1'`), and
returns an `Export`, whose `download`, `save`, `to` and `bytes` name the target last. An array or
an `Iterable` of rows writes every time. An `Iterator`, a generator included, is read once, so a second
write of its `Export` throws `LogicError` saying so.

**Rows go in batches, and compressed bytes come back.** `$sheet->add($row)` queues a row in the Novis
half, and a full batch crosses in one guest call, which returns the deflated bytes ready to leave; the
Novis half sends them on before it takes the next row. `addAll` takes any `iterable`, a generator or a
query result included, and batches it the same way. The guest writes sheet XML as plain text, deflates
it as it goes and frames each zip entry with a data descriptor, so it never knows an entry's size in
advance and never seeks. **Strings are written inline** (`t="inlineStr"`), so no shared-string table
grows with the sheet.

**Sheets are written one after another.** `$book->sheet('B')` finishes sheet A; writing to a finished
sheet throws naming it. `{position: n}` sets the tab order, which `workbook.xml` records at
`finish()`. A sheet name follows Excel's rules — at most 31 characters, none of `: \ / ? * [ ]`, not
empty, no leading or trailing apostrophe, unique in the workbook — and a bad one throws naming the
rule it broke.

**What stays changeable until the sheet is finished** is everything xlsx writes after the rows or in
a part of its own: merged ranges, hyperlinks, notes, data validation, outline groups, Excel tables,
conditional formats, images, charts, page setup and protection
([`core-classes/spreadsheet-sheet-end-parts`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-sheet-end-parts)). Each may point at any row already written. **What is
fixed before the first row** is what xlsx writes before the rows: frozen panes, column widths and
column styles, which is why they are sheet options and not calls. Row heights, hidden rows and outline
levels are options of `add`, because they are written with the row.

The sheet options are `columns` ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-styles-and-defaults`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-styles-and-defaults)), `header`,
`freeze`, `autofilter`, `headerStyle`, `position`, `hidden` (`true` or `'very'`), `tabColor`, `zoom`,
`gridlines`, `rightToLeft` and `overflow`. **The grid is Excel's**: row 1,048,577 throws naming the
limit, and `{overflow: 'newSheet'}` continues on a sheet named `<name> (2)` with the header row
repeated.

**`finish()`** writes the sheet-end parts, `styles.xml`, `workbook.xml`, the content types and the zip
directory, sends the last bytes, and returns a `Written`: the row count per sheet, the size in bytes,
and the bytes for `createInMemory`. **A download never finished is cut off and logged.**
`createForDownload` opens its stream with `Core\Response::stream`'s `$mustEnd` set to the download's
name, and `finish()` calls the stream's `end()`. When the program stops, however it stops, a stream
opened with `$mustEnd` and not ended has its body aborted, so the browser reports a failed download
and not a broken file, and one error record carrying the name as its `stream` field is written
(`nvs_runtime::Ctx::end_unfinished_stream`). No user code runs then
([`concurrency/cancellation-runs-no-user-code`](concurrency.md#concurrency-cancellation-runs-no-user-code)). It costs one pointer per request, and the name's
bytes for a request that streams a download. A workbook written to a file or to memory and never
finished is not reported. A CSV workbook writes each batch through `Core\Csv::format`, ignores styles,
widths and every sheet-end part, and throws naming the format when a second sheet is opened.

**An ods is held, not streamed.** ods puts data validation before the first sheet, and a merge, a
note, a link and an image inside the cells they cover, so a stream that had sent a sheet's rows could
not add them. The ods writer (`extensions/spreadsheet/src/ods/`) checks each row as xlsx does and keeps
it in the guest, compact, and `finish()` writes the whole package: `mimetype` first and stored, then
`content.xml`, `styles.xml`, `meta.xml`, `settings.xml` and the manifest. Every call before
`finish()` returns no bytes, so no byte of an ods leaves before it. A download's headers still leave
at create. Every style is an automatic style, one for each distinct combination, and a formula is
OpenFormula (`of:=`) with its cached value. Two writes of equal input are equal bytes, with `writer`'s
fixed dates.

The tradeoffs. **Performance:** one guest call per batch, not per cell, and a download starts before
the first row is written. **Usability:** an export is one line, and a stream from a query is a
`foreach`. **Simplicity:** one way to write, no editable mode, and the forward-only rules are these
paragraphs, written down once.

- **Memory:** per writing request, one batch of rows in the Novis half and its sheet XML in the guest,
  the compressor's window, the style combinations seen so far, and the sheet-end parts, all inside
  the request's cap and freed when the request ends. A million rows cost one batch, never the sheet,
  so a large export runs in the request and not in a queue.
- **Memory of an ods:** per writing request, every cell of the workbook, compact, under the request's
  cap and freed at `finish()`. **Latency of an ods:** the whole file leaves at `finish()`. A program
  that exports more rows than the cap holds writes xlsx or CSV.

**On disk.** The streaming writer (`extensions/spreadsheet/src/writer.rs`), the four targets,
`sheet`, `finish`, `Written`, `Sheet`'s `add` and `addAll` in batches of 1,000 rows, `fromRows` and
`Export` (`extensions/spreadsheet/nvs/Workbook.nvs`, `Sheet.nvs`, `Export.nvs`), with every sheet
option above, the sheet-name rules, the row options `height`, `hidden`, `level` and `style`,
`define`, CSV and ods (`extensions/spreadsheet/src/ods/`, `extensions/spreadsheet/src/book.rs`), and
the cut-off and logged download that was never finished
(`Core\Response::stream`'s `$mustEnd` and `Core\Response\Stream::end`,
`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/response.rs`).

**Declined:**
- **A request-end hook that calls `Stream::abort()`.** It runs user code after the handler returned,
  which cancellation forbids.
- **Dropping the promise.** The browser would save a broken file and nothing would say so.
- **An in-memory editable mode beside the stream.** Two ways to write is two sets of rules, and the
  editable one holds the whole sheet, which is the memory an export of user data must not cost.
- **`rust_xlsxwriter` as the writer.** Its constant-memory mode writes each sheet through a
  `std::fs::File`, which a guest with no preopen cannot open; it is a source of chart XML and of
  Excel-made fixtures only.
- **A shared-string table.** It grows with every distinct string, so a text-heavy export would hold
  all its text; inline strings cost a few bytes per cell on disk and nothing in memory.
- **Several sheets open at once.** Each would hold its own pending XML and compressor, and xlsx puts
  sheets in separate entries of one stream, so interleaving would buffer all but one.
- **Writing xls, and encrypted or password-protected files.** xls is a 1997 format nothing should
  produce, and encryption is not a sandboxed writer's job
  ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-evaluation-and-roster`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-evaluation-and-roster)).
- **Streaming ods, with the parts that cannot follow their rows refused.** A part that works in one
  format and throws in the other is two APIs. The held workbook costs memory, which is spent to keep
  one API.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/spreadsheet-roster`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-roster), [`core-classes/spreadsheet-sheet-end-parts`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-sheet-end-parts), [`core-classes/spreadsheet-styles-and-defaults`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-styles-and-defaults), [`core-classes/spreadsheet-bulk-boundary`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-bulk-boundary).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-spreadsheet-value-types"></a>

## Every Novis value writes as one cell type and every cell reads as one Novis type, and an `Instant` needs a zone

`rule:core-classes/spreadsheet-value-types`

Every Novis value writes as one cell type and every cell reads as one Novis type, by two fixed tables,
so neither a write nor a read guesses from the value's content.

**The write table:**

| Novis value | Cell |
|---|---|
| `string` | a text cell, always, whatever it begins with ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-formula-is-a-value`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-formula-is-a-value)) |
| `int`, `float` | a number; NaN and the infinities throw `LogicError` naming the column, for xlsx, ods and CSV alike |
| `decimal` | a number |
| `int` or `decimal` with more than 15 significant digits | a text cell, so no digit is lost |
| `bool` | `TRUE` or `FALSE` |
| `Date` | a serial with the format `yyyy-mm-dd` |
| `TimeOfDay` | a serial with the format `hh:mm:ss` |
| `Duration` | a serial with the format `[h]:mm:ss` |
| `DateTime` | its own clock time as a serial, with `yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm` |
| `Instant` | its clock time in the workbook's `zone`, with `yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm` |
| `null` | an empty cell |
| `Formula` | a formula, with its cached result when it carries one |
| `Cell::of($value, $style)` | the value's own cell, with that style on top of the row's and column's |

Any other value throws `LogicError` naming the column and the type. A column or `Style` `format`
replaces the table's format and never the cell type.

**The zone rule.** A serial has no zone, so an `Instant` needs one to become a clock time: the
workbook's `zone` option, and with none the write throws naming the column. A `DateTime` already
carries its clock time, which is written as it is. On read, `zone` (default `'UTC'`) is the zone a
read `DateTime` is placed in, and the clock time in the file is kept exactly; no conversion moves it.

**The read table:**

| Cell | Novis value |
|---|---|
| text, inline or shared | `string` |
| a whole number within ±2^53 | `int` |
| another number | `float` |
| `TRUE`, `FALSE` | `bool` |
| a number with a date format that has a date and a time | `DateTime` in `zone` |
| a number with a date format that has no time | `Date` |
| a number with a format that has only a time | `TimeOfDay` |
| a number with an elapsed-time format (`[h]`, `[mm]`, `[ss]`) | `Duration` |
| an error value | a `CellError` case |
| empty | `null` |
| a formula | its stored result, read by this table; `{formulas: true}` gives the `Formula` with that result as its `cached` |

A format is a date format when its code has a date or time token outside quotes and brackets, or it is
one of the built-in ids that are. Both epochs are read, 1900 with its leap-day bug and 1904.
`{text: [...]}` names columns that read as Excel's displayed text instead, and `{text: true}` reads
every column so ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-reads-as-a-stream`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-reads-as-a-stream)). A CSV cell is always `string`,
because CSV has no other type.

The tradeoffs. **Usability:** an import gets an `int` where the sheet has a whole number and a `Date`
where it has a date, with no parse in the program. **Simplicity:** one table per direction, and the
display text is one option away when the table is not what the program wants.

**On disk.** The write table, `Cell::of` and the zone rule: the Novis half picks a value's case
(`extensions/spreadsheet/nvs/Workbook.nvs`) and the component writes it
(`extensions/spreadsheet/src/cells.rs`). The read table and `{text: ...}`
(`extensions/spreadsheet/src/read/mod.rs`, `extensions/spreadsheet/src/format/mod.rs`).

**Declined:**
- **A `string` that looks like a number written as a number.** The cell would depend on the content,
  and a zip code or an account number would lose its leading zeros.
- **Writing an `Instant` in UTC when no `zone` is set.** Every reader in another zone would see the
  wrong clock time with nothing to tell them; a throw names the missing option once.
- **Reading every number as `float`.** An id column would come back as `1042.0`, and ±2^53 is exactly
  the range in which `float` holds a whole number without loss.
- **A read `DateTime` converted into the program's zone.** The file holds a clock time and no zone, so
  any conversion would invent the zone it converts from.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/spreadsheet-formula-is-a-value`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-formula-is-a-value), [`core-classes/spreadsheet-reads-as-a-stream`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-reads-as-a-stream), [`core-classes/spreadsheet-writes-as-a-stream`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-writes-as-a-stream).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-spreadsheet-formula-is-a-value"></a>

## Only an explicit `Formula` value writes a formula cell, so an export built from user data is inert

`rule:core-classes/spreadsheet-formula-is-a-value`

Only an explicit `Formula` value produces a formula cell. Every string writes as a **text cell** —
including one beginning `=`, `+`, `-`, `@` or a control character, which is the whole trigger set for
the formula-injection class.

An export built from user data is therefore inert by construction rather than by a caller remembering
to prefix a quote. This is the same move taint tracking makes everywhere else — code and data
separated by type, not by inspection — applied at a boundary that is otherwise a footnote in a
security advisory. Because the writer cannot be tricked into emitting code, it needs no launderer. A
template fill holds to the same rule: a value beginning `=` fills as text
([`core-classes/spreadsheet-template-fill`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-template-fill)).

**A formula is plain Excel text**, `Formula::of('SUM(C2:C9)', {cached: 42})`, with no placeholder syntax
inside it. Three helpers write the references, so a program never computes a column letter:

- `$sheet->cell($key, $row)` is the A1 address of the column `$key` (a column key or a letter) in row
  `$row`, such as `C7`.
- `$sheet->column($key)` is the column's data range over the rows written so far, such as `C2:C1043`,
  so a totals row written after the data covers every row of the stream.
- A column's `formula: fn(int $row) => Formula` is called once per row with that row's number, and its
  `Formula` is the column's cell in that row.

**A formula has 1 to 8,192 characters** once its leading `=` is dropped, Excel's limit. One check
(`cells::check_formula`) holds every formula the writer writes: a `Formula` cell, a column's formula,
a table total, a conditional format and a validation. `Formula::of('')` throws `LogicError` in the
Novis half, before any row is written.

`cached` is the result the file carries beside the formula, for a reader that does not recalculate;
with none, the cell has no cached value. Every written workbook is flagged to recalculate when it is
opened, so Excel shows computed values whatever was cached.

What it costs is one wrapper at the call sites that genuinely mean a formula, which is the smaller
half of any real export.

The component's tests owe a `tainted` string beginning `=` that lands as a text cell, and the same
expression as a `Formula` value that lands as a formula cell, both asserted on the written bytes
rather than the builder's state.

**On disk.** `Formula`, the three helpers and the text-cell rule
(`extensions/spreadsheet/nvs/Formula.nvs`, `Sheet.nvs`).

**Declined:**
- **Placeholders inside formula text, such as `{qty}*{price}`.** It is a second syntax inside Excel's,
  and the helpers give the same references as Novis strings.
- **A string beginning `=` written as a formula, with an escape for text.** Every export of user data
  would then be one forgotten escape from injection.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/spreadsheet-has-no-io`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-has-no-io), [`core-classes/spreadsheet-evaluation-and-roster`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-evaluation-and-roster).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-spreadsheet-styles-and-defaults"></a>

## A `Style` layers column, row and cell, and a sheet with a header row is bold, bordered, frozen, filtered and auto-width by default

`rule:core-classes/spreadsheet-styles-and-defaults`

A style is a `Style::of({...})` value, layered column, then row, then cell, and a sheet with a header
row is styled by default: a bold header with a bottom border, frozen, filtered, and every column
`width: 'auto'`.

**The style fields**, every one optional:

| Field | Values |
|---|---|
| `font` | a font name, such as `'Calibri'` |
| `size` | points, a `float` |
| `bold`, `italic`, `strike` | `bool` |
| `underline` | `true`, `'single'` or `'double'` |
| `color`, `fill` | `'#RRGGBB'` |
| `border` | `'thin'`, `'medium'`, `'thick'`, `'dashed'`, `'dotted'` or `'double'` on every side, or `{top?, right?, bottom?, left?}` of those |
| `borderColor` | `'#RRGGBB'` |
| `align` | `'left'`, `'center'`, `'right'`, `'fill'` or `'justify'` |
| `valign` | `'top'`, `'center'` or `'bottom'` |
| `wrap` | `bool` |
| `rotate` | degrees, -90 to 90 |
| `indent` | an `int` |
| `format` | a format code, or a shortcut below |
| `locked`, `hideFormula` | `bool`, which take effect only on a protected sheet |

**The format shortcuts** are `'date'` (`yyyy-mm-dd`), `'datetime'` (`yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm`), `'time'`
(`hh:mm:ss`), `'duration'` (`[h]:mm:ss`), `'integer'` (`0`), `'decimal'` (`0.00`), `'money'`
(`#,##0.00`), `'percent'` (`0%`) and `'text'` (`@`). Any other string is a format code, written as it
is.

**Layering.** A cell's style is each field from the most specific layer that sets it: the cell's own
(`Cell::of`), then the row's (`add`'s `style`), then the column's. A field no layer sets is Excel's
default. Every distinct combination becomes one entry of `styles.xml` at `finish()`, so equal
combinations share one entry, and Excel's limit of 65,490 cell formats throws naming it.

**Columns** are a sheet option, `columns: {key: {...}}`, keyed by the row's array keys, in the order the
header is written. A column takes `header` (its header text, default the key), `width` (characters,
or `'auto'`), `format`, `style`, `hidden` and `formula`
([`core-classes/spreadsheet-formula-is-a-value`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-formula-is-a-value)). A row key no column names is written after the
named ones in the order of the first row; a column a row lacks is an empty cell. Rows that are lists
of plain lists have no keys, so they have no header and no defaults.

**The defaults, whenever a sheet has a header row**, in `fromRows` and `sheet()` alike: the header row
bold with a thin bottom border (`headerStyle`), frozen below it (`freeze`), with an autofilter over the
header and its `_xlnm._FilterDatabase` name, as Excel writes one (`autofilter`), and every column `width: 'auto'`. Each turns off on its own:
`{freeze: false, autofilter: false, headerStyle: false}`, or a column's own `width`. `headerStyle` is
`false` and not `null`, the way `freeze` and `autofilter` are, because an options field set to `null`
reads the same as one left out. `headerStyle: Style::of({...})` replaces the default style. `header:
false` writes no header row, and so none of these.

**Auto width** measures the header and the rows the Novis half holds before the first chunk leaves —
the first 1,000 — or every row when `fromRows` is given an array. A cell's width is its text as Excel
displays it, through the number-format renderer the reader's `text` option uses, counting a wide East
Asian character as two, plus one, capped at 60. There are no font metrics.

The tradeoffs. **Usability:** an export looks finished with no option at all, and a style is a value
a program names once and reuses. **Performance:** the 1,000-row window keeps a download's first byte
from waiting on the whole query. **Memory:** the window is up to 1,000 rows held once, at the start of
a sheet.

- **Memory:** per writing request, one entry per distinct style combination until `finish()`, and the
  auto-width window of at most 1,000 rows before the first chunk leaves.

**On disk.** `Style::of`, `Cell::of`, the row's `style`, `columns` with `header`, `width`, `format`,
`style`, `hidden` and `formula`, the header row and its four defaults, and auto width through the
number-format renderer (`extensions/spreadsheet/nvs/Workbook.nvs`, `Style.nvs`,
`extensions/spreadsheet/src/width.rs`). A style's fields hold the enums `Style::Line`,
`Style::Underline`, `Style::Align` and `Style::Valign`, which `Style::of` makes from their strings.

**Declined:**
- **A style as an options bag on every call, with no value.** A report repeats the same few styles on
  thousands of rows, and a value compares and dedupes once.
- **Unstyled by default.** The common export is a table with a header, and the four defaults are
  what every user would otherwise add by hand.
- **Auto width over every row of a stream.** It would hold the sheet until the end, which is the memory
  streaming exists to avoid.
- **Font metrics for auto width.** It needs every font's tables in the guest for a width a reader
  changes with one drag; characters as displayed are close enough, and the cap keeps one long cell
  from taking the screen.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/spreadsheet-writes-as-a-stream`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-writes-as-a-stream), [`core-classes/spreadsheet-value-types`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-value-types).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-spreadsheet-sheet-end-parts"></a>

## Merges, links, notes, validation, tables, conditional formats, images and charts may point at any written row until the sheet ends

`rule:core-classes/spreadsheet-sheet-end-parts`

The parts xlsx writes after a sheet's rows or in a part of its own are `Sheet` calls that may point at
any row already written, until the sheet is finished: merged ranges, hyperlinks, notes, data
validation, outline groups, Excel tables, conditional formats, images, charts, page setup and
protection.

| Call | What it writes |
|---|---|
| `merge(string $range)` | a merged range |
| `link(string $cell, string $target, {text?, tooltip?})` | a hyperlink to a URL, a `mailto:` address or `'Sheet!A1'` |
| `note(string $cell, string $text, {author?})` | a note |
| `validate(string $range, {...})` | data validation: `list`, `whole`, `decimal`, `date` or `length` with `between`, `min` or `max`, or `formula`; `input` and `error` messages; `allowEmpty` |
| `group(string $rows, {collapsed?})` | an outline group over `'5:9'` or `'B:D'` |
| `table(string $range, {name?, style?, banded?, filter?, totals?})` | an Excel table; `totals` maps a column to `'sum'`, `'average'`, `'count'`, `'min'`, `'max'` or a `Formula`, and the table's own formulas may use structured references such as `[@qty]` |
| `conditional(string $range, {...})` | one conditional format: `cell` with an operator and values, `formula`, `colorScale`, `dataBar`, `iconSet`, `top` or `bottom` N, `duplicates` or `unique`, each with a `style` of font, fill, border and format |
| `image(string $cell, bytes $data, {width?, height?, offsetX?, offsetY?})` | a PNG, JPEG or GIF, read from its bytes; any other format, a PNG cut before its `IEND` chunk, and an image that ends past column `XFD` or row 1,048,576 throw `LogicError` |
| `chart(string $cell, Chart $chart, {width?, height?})` | a chart of the subset below; one that ends past the grid throws `LogicError` |
| `print({...})` | page setup: `orientation`, `fitToPage`, `margins`, `header`, `footer`, `repeatRows`, `area`, in one call; a second `print` on the sheet throws `LogicError` |
| `protect({password?, allow?})` | sheet protection |

Row heights, hidden rows and outline levels are `add`'s options, and hidden columns a column's
([`core-classes/spreadsheet-styles-and-defaults`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-styles-and-defaults)), because xlsx writes them with the row or before
it. For the same reason a `group` over rows is added before those rows, a `group` over columns and
`print`'s `fitToPage` before the sheet's first row, and each throws `LogicError` saying so when it
comes later. **A link goes to `http:`, `https:`, `mailto:` or a cell of the workbook**, and any
other target, such as `file:` or `javascript:`, throws `LogicError`, so a link built from user data
opens no local file and runs nothing. `Workbook::define` writes a defined name, and the workbook's
`properties` the document properties.
Rich text in one cell is `Cell::rich`. **Sheet protection locks the layout and is not security**: the
password is a hash any tool removes, which the reference card says.

**An image is its own zip entry.** One added before the sheet's first row is written by the call that
adds it. Once the rows have started, the sheet's own entry is open, and a zip entry cannot be split,
so the image's bytes wait until the sheet ends. A report with many images adds them before its rows,
or on a sheet of their own, to hold none of them.

**A table's top row is its header row**, and each column is named by its header cell, which needs a
name different from the others. Once rows are written only the sheet's header row is kept, so a
table added after its rows starts at that row, and one added earlier takes its names when the row is
written. **The totals row is the row after the table**: a table added after its last row writes it
at once, and one added earlier writes it right after its last row, so the program's next row comes
after it. A sheet that ends before a table's header row or totals row throws `LogicError`. A total
is `SUBTOTAL` over the column, which skips the rows a filter hides. `[@qty]` and `[qty]` are
qualified by the table's name in the totals row and in every row written after the table is added;
a row written before it keeps its formula text as given. The sheet's default autofilter is left out
where a table covers it, and a table overlaps no merged range and no other table.

**A conditional format's values are formula text**, so a text value is quoted. Its rules take
priority in the order they are added. A rule that formats cells needs a `style`, of which the font's
bold, italic, strike, underline and colour, the fill, the border and the format apply; a colour
scale, a data bar and an icon set take `colors` instead, and a `style` on one throws `LogicError`.
**The chart subset** is column, bar, line, area, pie, doughnut and scatter, and a
combination of two different types of column, line and area over one pair of axes, with a title,
axis titles, the legend, series colours and data labels. Any other combination throws `LogicError`.
A series names its ranges with `$sheet->column($key)`, so a chart over a stream covers every row the
sheet ends with: the chart is written when the sheet ends, and a range on its own sheet that ends at
the row `column` gives when the chart is added ends at the sheet's last row. Any other range is
written as given, and the chart holds no values. A series range is read by the reference parser
`Workbook::define` uses, without whole columns or rows ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-output-is-inert`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-output-is-inert)),
so a range into another workbook, a URL, an unclosed quote or a second sheet name throws
`LogicError` naming the range. A title or an axis title past 255 characters throws. **A series' categories are a number reference**
when they are a column of the chart's own sheet whose every value below its header is a number or a date, which the
writer knows from one flag per column kept as rows pass, and a text reference otherwise. Its XML
follows `rust_xlsxwriter`'s output for the same chart, ported for the subset and attributed in the
module that writes it.

**An image or a chart is anchored from its cell to the cell its size ends at**, as Excel anchors
one, with that cell's offset. The end cell needs the width of every column and the height of every
row the anchor spans, and an anchor may be added after its rows have left. So the writer keeps the
open sheet's custom row heights, one entry per run of rows with the same height. A sheet with no
custom height keeps nothing, and an anchor added before its rows finds its end cell as they pass.

**An ods carries the same parts, with the same checks and errors**, written where ODF 1.3 puts them
(`extensions/spreadsheet/src/ods/`). A merge spans its first cell and covers the rest, a link is a
`text:a` in the cell's text, a note an `office:annotation` in the cell, and an image a `draw:frame`
in its cell with the picture under `Pictures/`. Data validation is `table:content-validations` before
the first sheet. Outline groups are `table:table-row-group` and `table:table-column-group`, page
setup a page layout and master page in `styles.xml`, and protection `table:protected` with Excel's
hash as its key. A table is a `table:database-range`, and a conditional format LibreOffice's
`calcext:conditional-formats`. A table's style and banding have no ods form and are left out, and a
structured reference is written as the cells it names. A protected sheet's `allow` names have no ods
form either. A chart is an embedded chart object, `Object <n>/content.xml` with one `chart:chart`,
written from the same checked chart as in xlsx (`extensions/spreadsheet/src/ods/chart.rs`). Its
`draw:frame` with a `draw:object` is in the anchor cell, beside the images in the order they were
added, and the manifest names the object. A combination is one plot area whose series each name
their type. A series name is LibreOffice's `loext:label-string`, because ODF 1.3 names a series only
by a cell. As in xlsx, the object keeps no values, and a range that ends at the column's last row
grows with the sheet.

The tradeoffs. **Usability:** a report's merges, totals and chart are written after the rows they
summarise, in the order a program computes them. **Memory:** the parts are held until the sheet ends,
and they are small beside the rows.

- **Memory:** per writing request, each sheet-end part of the open sheet until the sheet is finished,
  and the bytes of each image added after the sheet's first row, until the sheet is finished.
- **Memory:** per writing request, the open sheet's custom row heights, 8 bytes per run of rows with
  the same height, and one flag per column, until the sheet is finished. A sheet with no custom height
  keeps none, and one whose every row differs from the row before keeps 8 MB at Excel's 1,048,576 rows.

**On disk.** Every sheet-end part above, called from `extensions/spreadsheet/nvs/Sheet.nvs` and
written by `extensions/spreadsheet/src/tail.rs`, `table.rs`, `conditional.rs`, `drawing.rs` and
`chart.rs`.

**Declined:**
- **Pivot tables, sparklines and threaded comments.** Each is a part with its own cache or model, for
  a feature a reader builds in Excel from the data in seconds.
- **Every chart type outside the subset, trendlines, error bars, secondary axes beyond the
  combination, chartsheets and 3D.** The subset is what reports use; the rest is Excel's to add.
- **An image that is not PNG, JPEG or GIF converted on the way in.** `Novis\Image` converts it in one
  call, and the writer stays a writer.
- **A chart's cached values, the `numCache` and `strCache` Excel writes beside each reference.** A
  chart added after its rows finds them gone, so a cache would mean keeping every cell of every sheet,
  and one only for a chart added first would make the file depend on call order. Excel and LibreOffice
  read the cells when they open the file, and every workbook is flagged to recalculate. A viewer that
  draws from the cache alone shows the chart empty. The Excel comparison removes the caches from
  Excel's file and names that in its harness.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/spreadsheet-writes-as-a-stream`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-writes-as-a-stream), [`core-classes/spreadsheet-formula-is-a-value`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-formula-is-a-value).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-spreadsheet-template-fill"></a>

## A template fill copies every part but the filled cells, repeats the rows a list marks, and shifts every reference below them

`rule:core-classes/spreadsheet-template-fill`

`Template::open($source)->fill($data)` copies every part of a designed workbook unchanged except the
cells it fills, writes a row marked by a list once per item, and moves every reference below it so the
formulas, tables and charts still point at the right rows.

**Placeholders** are `{{name}}` and `{{customer.name}}`, a path into `$data`'s keys. A cell that is
only a placeholder takes the value's cell type by [`core-classes/spreadsheet-value-types`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-value-types)'s write
table and keeps the cell's style; a placeholder with text around it makes the cell text. A string
value beginning `=` stays text ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-formula-is-a-value`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-formula-is-a-value)). A date, a time
or a duration filled into a cell whose style shows no date or time gets the write table's format for
its type: `styles.xml` gains one `cellXfs` entry for each style and format pair, so the value reads as
a date in Excel and in the reader. Formula text holds no placeholder: a formula refers to the cells
that do.

**What throws at `fill`, before any byte is written.** A placeholder outside a list's rows that the
data lacks throws `LogicError` naming it and its cell, on whichever sheet it stands; a list item's
own placeholders are checked as its items are written. A flat key `'customer.name'` and a nested
`customer` → `name` give one path, and throw naming both keys: a path never picks one of them in
silence. The engine's fill call with one list named twice throws naming the list, and its items call
with a list the fill did not return throws naming it.

**Repeated rows.** A row whose placeholder goes through a list, `{{items.qty}}`, is written once per
item of `$data['items']`, each copy with the template row's style and height. A block of several rows
repeats as one when a defined name equal to the list's name covers it, so an item can span two rows.
**A list inside a list throws**, naming both. An item whose copy would end past row 1,048,576 throws
`LogicError` naming the list, before any of its rows is written. **A list is an array or an
`Iterator`**, such as a generator. The items go to the component in batches of 1,000 whichever it
is, and an `Iterator` is read only while the file is written, so a list of any length on a sheet that
streams costs one batch.

**Lists on several sheets.** Each sheet may repeat its own lists, and the sheets with lists are
written in workbook order, each with its own shifts. The lists are filled in the order their blocks
stand: sheet order, then row. A block's shift moves every reference to its rows, from its own sheet
and from every other sheet and part. A sheet waits for its items, and is written when the fill
finishes, when a formula above one of its blocks names a row that block moves, or when a formula or
part on it names a row a list on a later sheet moves. It then costs the memory of its items.

**The shift.** Every row below a repeated block moves down by the rows it added, and every part that
points at those rows moves with it: merged ranges, formulas, defined names, the print area, the
autofilter, data validation, conditional formats (an `x14` one under `extLst` too), tables, drawing
anchors and chart ranges. A shared formula (`<f t="shared">`) whose first cell is in a block gets a
new group number (`si`) in every copy but the first, numbered after the sheet's highest, so no two
copies share one; a group whose first cell is outside the block keeps its number. A range
that covers the template row grows with the block, so `SUM(C5:C5)` over a block of 100 items becomes
`SUM(C5:C104)`. The shifter tokenizes A1 references — relative, absolute, ranges, whole rows and
columns, and references to other sheets — and leaves every other character of formula text as it was.

**`->set('Summary!B2', $value)`** fills one cell by address, by the same write table, before `fill`.
An address with no sheet name, `set('B2', …)`, is on the first sheet. A filled value's text is
escaped as every written cell's is, so a NUL is written `_x0000_`.
`fill` returns an `Export`, so the target is the last call: `->download($name)`, `->save($path)`,
`->to($file)` or `->bytes()`. The source is a `Core\IO\File` or `bytes`, read as
[`core-classes/spreadsheet-reads-as-a-stream`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-reads-as-a-stream) reads one. **The source is never `tainted`:** the
filled file carries the template's own formulas, links and sheets unescaped, so filling is safe only
with a template the program trusts. A program filling an upload says so with
`Core\Taint::assertTrusted($bytes, $reason)` itself, and with a plain source no taint reaches the
written file, so the `Export` stays plain `bytes`. **An xlsm template gives xlsx**: the
`vbaProject` part and its relationship are dropped, and the content type is the xlsx one
([`core-classes/spreadsheet-output-is-inert`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-output-is-inert)). Two fills of equal input are byte-equal.

The tradeoffs. **Usability:** a designer builds the invoice in Excel, and the program supplies data.
**Simplicity:** one placeholder syntax, one list rule and no list inside a list. **Performance and
memory:** the repeated rows stream, so a template of a thousand items costs what one batch does.

- **Memory:** per filling request, the parts the template carries that are not sheet rows (the styles,
  the drawings, the parts the shift rewrites), the template's sheet rows as they stream through, and
  one batch of repeated rows, freed when the request ends.

**On disk.** `Template::open`, `set` and `fill`, and an `Export` from `fill` to all four targets
(`extensions/spreadsheet/nvs/Template.nvs`, `extensions/spreadsheet/src/template/`).

**Declined:**
- **A list inside a list.** It needs nested blocks whose shifts compound, for a layout almost nobody
  designs; a program that needs it writes the sheet with `Workbook`.
- **Placeholders inside formula text.** A formula that names a filled cell does the same job, and
  text substituted into a formula is the injection the formula rule closes.
- **`umya-spreadsheet` as the filler.** It loads the whole workbook into an editable model, which is
  the memory a template with a long list must not cost.
- **`Template::open` taking `tainted bytes`.** An uploaded template's formulas and external links
  reach the filled file as written, and taint flowing through the engine would make every export
  `tainted bytes`; the one explicit `assertTrusted` at the upload is the honest place for the trust.
- **Keeping the macros of an xlsm template.** The writer emits no executable content
  ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-output-is-inert`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-output-is-inert)).

<sub>See also [`core-classes/spreadsheet-value-types`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-value-types), [`core-classes/spreadsheet-output-is-inert`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-output-is-inert), [`core-classes/spreadsheet-formula-is-a-value`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-formula-is-a-value).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-spreadsheet-reads-as-a-stream"></a>

## xlsx and xlsb are read through byte ranges a host import serves from the lent source, into typed rows keyed by their row numbers
