`rule:core-classes/spreadsheet-reads-as-a-stream`

`Reader::open($source)` reads a `Core\IO\File` the program opened, or `bytes` it holds, and xlsx and
xlsb are read as a stream of byte ranges, so a 100 MB upload never enters the guest whole; xlsm, xls
and ods are read whole, and CSV goes to `Core\Csv`.

**How the guest reads a range.** Every reader call lends the source as a `mixed` value, and the guest
reads ranges of it through a host import, an accessor of the `value` handle that returns the bytes at
an offset and length of a `bytes` value or of an open `Core\IO\File`. The source is lent by number
and never copied as it crosses: the host serves each range from the program's own `bytes`, or
reads it from the file and puts the handle's position back, between two polls of the call, and
gives at most 1 MiB per range. The guest keeps a read-ahead
buffer, reads the zip directory from the end, and inflates each part as it parses it. The import
grants nothing: it reads only what the program lent to this call, and the handle stops being valid
when the call returns ([`packaging/values-cross-as-handles`](packaging.md#packaging-values-cross-as-handles)), so the source is lent again on every
call. This is chosen against a pull loop in the Novis half, in which the guest would return "bytes
needed at offset N, length L" and the Novis code would read them and call again, for two reasons. On
request latency, the import costs one host call per read-ahead block and runs no Novis code between
them, where the pull loop costs a guest return, a Novis read and a guest call for every block. And
the parsers read synchronously, the readers of the whole formats included, and a pull loop would
need every parser rewritten as a resumable state machine.

**A reader reads only the file it opened.** `readerOpen` keeps the source's size and a 64-bit
FNV-1a hash of its first and last 512 bytes, and every other reader export checks them first
(`extensions/spreadsheet/src/read/mod.rs`'s `Reader::check`). Another source, or a file changed on
disk since the open, throws `LogicError`. A zip keeps its directory at its end and a compound file
its header at its start, so a replaced workbook changes its size or one of its ends. Cost: two
reads of 512 bytes per call, on a call that reads at least a batch of rows or a part. `readerRows`
with `max` 0 throws `LogicError`. `properties()` reads its parts at its first call and keeps them,
so they count against the byte bound once. Memory: the properties' text, per reader.

**Formats** are told apart by their bytes: a zip is xlsx or xlsm when its workbook part is XML,
xlsb when it is `xl/workbook.bin`, and ods when it has a `content.xml` and no workbook part. An OLE
compound file is xls. Other bytes are CSV when they are text: they start with a UTF-16 byte order
mark, `csv`'s `encoding` names their charset, or their first 4 KiB have no NUL byte and no control
character but tab, line feed, form feed and carriage return. Anything else throws `ParseError`,
naming the formats the reader reads. xls holds at most 65,536 rows, and an xls from
Excel 95 or earlier, BIFF5 and before, throws naming it. An xlsm's macros are listed by `macros()`
and never run: the VBA project's `dir` stream is decompressed and its module names read, and no
module's code is read. An xls's project is its `_VBA_PROJECT_CUR` storage, and an xlsm's is the part
the workbook's relationships name, or `xl/vbaProject.bin` when none does, so a file never hides one.

**xls and ods are read whole** when the reader opens: the file is held in the guest, and every
sheet's rows with it. An xls's formulas are decoded from their tokens when the file opens, as
**Formulas from every format** below says. An ods stores a formula as OpenFormula text, which the
reader translates to A1 text (`extensions/spreadsheet/src/openformula.rs`), so its cell gives a
`Formula` as an xlsx cell does; a formula the translator cannot read gives none. An ods cell carries its
type in its own attributes, and a time value in it reads as a `TimeOfDay` under 24 hours and a
`Duration` from 24 hours on. A row or a cell with a repeat count is that many, an empty one costs
nothing, and a repeat past the grid throws. An ods cell's `text` is rendered under the file's own
`number:*-style`, which the reader translates to a format code
(`extensions/spreadsheet/src/read/ods_styles.rs`), found through the cell's style, its row's or
its column's default style, and each style's parents.

**`rows($sheet, {...})`** takes the sheet by name or by position from 0 and yields one `Row` per row:
its `number` is the **row number in the file**, and its `values` the row's array. The row number is
not the `foreach` key, because a cursor carries no key ([`iteration/foreach-subjects`](iteration.md#iteration-foreach-subjects)), and a
generator yields a class and not a shape. The generator reads each batch the engine returns and
yields its rows, so a read holds one batch at a time.

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `header` | `false` | `true` reads the first row with a value at or after `from` as the header; an `int` names the header's row number. The values are then keyed by header text |
| `from` | the first row | the first row number to read |
| `limit` | none | the most rows to yield |
| `columns` | every column | `['A:C', 'F']` |
| `zone` | `'UTC'` | the zone a read `DateTime` is in |
| `text` | none | the columns, by header or letter, that read as their displayed text; `true` for all |
| `formulas` | `false` | `true` reads a formula cell as its `Formula` |
| `emptyRows` | `'skip'` | `'keep'` yields an empty row. A row with no cell is empty; a formula cell with no cached value is a cell, which reads as `null`, or as its `Formula` with `cached` `null` under `formulas: true` |
| `merged` | `'first'` | `'fill'` gives every cell of a merged range its value |
| `hidden` | `'read'` | `'skip'` leaves hidden rows out |
| `locale` | `'en'` | the separators and the month and day names `text` renders with. A tag whose language the reader has no names for throws `LogicError` naming it. The built-in formats 14 and 22 render as Excel shows them in en-US, `m/d/yyyy` and `m/d/yyyy h:mm`, whatever the locale: Excel is the reference, and SheetJS's `m/d/yy` is not |

**Merged ranges.** `merged($sheet)` gives a sheet's ranges as A1 text, `'A1:C2'`, in the file's
order. An xlsx or xlsb sheet lists them after its rows, so the call reads the sheet's part to its
end; an xls or ods has them from the open. Without a fill, a range's value is in its top-left cell
only. **`merged: 'fill'` reads the ranges before the first row**, at that one more pass over the
part, and gives every cell of a range the top-left value, the cells outside `columns` dropped after.
A filled cell in a `text` column reads as the top-left cell's displayed text.
A row the file does not write is yielded when it lies in a range below its top row. A range whose
top-left cell is above `from` still fills the rows below it, because the cursor reads every row
from the first. A range past the grid throws. The fill keeps each range, 32 bytes, and the top-left
value of each range the read is inside, and drops a range once the read passes its last row, so a
row costs the ranges it is in and not every range of the sheet. The header row is never filled.

With a header, **every row has every header key**, and a missing cell is `null`; a duplicate header
gets ` (2)`, ` (3)` and on, and an empty header cell is its column letter. Without one, a row is keyed
by column letter. A CSV read takes the same options and gives the same row shape, and its cells are
all `string`.

**`sheets()`** gives one shape per sheet: `name`, `position`, `visibility` (`Reader::Visibility`), `rows`
and `columns` as the file declares them, and `kind` (`Reader::SheetKind`, `Worksheet` or `Chartsheet`).
A sheet that declares no dimension, or only `A1`, is counted from its rows: the last row with a cell
and the last column of any row. The first call reads every sheet's facts, and the reader keeps them
for every later call. Memory: a name and a few numbers per sheet, per reader. Every method that takes
a sheet takes `tainted string|int`, so a name from `sheets()` goes back as it is: the name is only
compared with the file's own sheet names. **The extras
read on request**, each for one sheet or the workbook: `merged`, `links`, `notes`, `names`, `tables`,
`images` (as bytes with their anchor), `properties` and `macros`. An external link, a linked image or a
data connection reads as data and is never followed ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-has-no-io`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-has-no-io)): a
hyperlink is its target's text with `external` set, a linked picture has no bytes and its target's
text in `link`, and a defined name over another workbook is its reference's text. A picture is listed
at the top-left cell of its anchor, and one anchored to no cell is not listed. `properties()` gives
`created` as an `Instant`. Hyperlinks are read from the sheet's part to its end, as `merged` is, and
the other extras from parts small enough to read whole. An ods's extras are read with its cells: a
link is a `text:a` in a cell, a note an `office:annotation`, a picture a `draw:frame` in a cell, a
name a `table:named-range` or `table:named-expression` (local to the sheet whose table holds it),
and a table a `table:database-range`, the range LibreOffice keeps for a sheet's own filter
excepted. Its properties are `meta.xml`'s, with the initial creator as the author.

**Shared strings are kept in one arena** with `u32` offsets, never one allocation per entry, and the
reader reads `styles.xml`'s number formats and each cell's style index, which the read table's date
rule and the `text` option need. **A part streamed and never held** — a sheet read row by row — is
bounded by the decompression ratio alone; a part held whole, such as the shared strings, keeps both
bounds ([`core-classes/decompression-bound`](core-classes.md#core-classes-decompression-bound)).

The tradeoffs. **Performance:** one host call per read-ahead block, one guest call per batch of rows,
and no Novis code between blocks. **Usability:** typed values, the header's keys on every row, and row
numbers to report errors by. **Simplicity:** one `Reader` for every format, CSV included. **Memory:**
spent on the shared strings, which a file may make large, and bounded by the request's cap.

- **Memory:** per reading request, the read-ahead buffer, the inflater's window, one batch of rows,
  the number formats, and the shared strings of the file being read in one arena; for xlsm, xls and
  ods, the whole file; with `merged: 'fill'`, the sheet's ranges. All of it is inside the request's
  cap and freed when the request ends.

**The Novis half** asks for 1,000 rows a call, with `from` one past the last row it was given.
`header: true` costs one call more, for the number of the first row with a value. Text read from a
file is `tainted`, so a `Formula` read with `formulas: true` carries a number result and not a text
one. The engine's resource is `reading`, because a manifest's resource is a class in
`Novis\Spreadsheet` and `Reader` is the class over it.

**Formulas from every format.** With `formulas: true`, a formula cell of every format gives a
`Formula` with its A1 text. xls and xlsb store a formula as parsed tokens, which one decoder turns
into the text an xlsx cell writes (`extensions/spreadsheet/src/read/tokens.rs`): every operand and
operator token, Excel's built-in function table, an add-in call such as `_xlfn.XLOOKUP`, an array
constant, a defined name and a reference to another sheet. A reference into another workbook is
`[1]Shop!A1` and its name `[1]!Rate`, as an xlsx cell writes them, numbered in the order the file
lists the other workbooks. Their sheet names are an xls `SUPBOOK`'s, and for an xlsb the
`BrtSupTabs` of the external link part its `BrtSupBookSrc` names, read for those names alone. A
shared formula is decoded for each
cell it covers, with its relative references moved by that cell's distance from its first cell.
An xls is decoded when the file opens, and an xlsb as its rows are read. A token the decoder does
not know, a structured reference in an xlsb and a name it cannot find give no `Formula`, and the cell reads as its stored result. What it spends: the
text of each formula of an xls, held with its rows, and for an xlsb the sheets, the `XTI` list and
the names, read with the workbook part when the file opens.

**On disk.** `Reader::open`, `sheets()`, `rows()` and the extras read xlsx, xlsm, xlsb, xls, ods
and CSV, from `bytes` or an open `Core\IO\File` (`extensions/spreadsheet/nvs/Reader.nvs`,
`extensions/spreadsheet/src/read/`). A CSV is read by `Core\Csv` in the Novis half
([`core-classes/spreadsheet-has-no-io`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-has-no-io)).

**The extras of an xlsb** are read from its records: a hyperlink is a `BrtHLink` of the sheet part,
a note is in a comments part of records, a table is the `BrtBeginList` of its part, and a defined
name is a `BrtName` of the workbook part, whose formula the token decoder turns into its text. The
drawing and the relationships are XML, as in an xlsx (`extensions/spreadsheet/src/read/extras.rs`).

**The extras of an xls** are read with its cells: a hyperlink is a `HLINK` record with its
`HLINKTOOLTIP`, a note is a `NOTE` whose text is the `TXO` after the `OBJ` of the same id, and a
defined name is a `NAME` of the globals, whose formula the token decoder turns into its text. A
picture is a shape of the sheet's `MSODRAWING` records, its bytes in the picture store of the
globals' `MSODRAWINGGROUP` and its cell its client anchor's. The properties are the
`\x05SummaryInformation` and `\x05DocumentSummaryInformation` streams. BIFF8 has no table part, so
`tables` gives an empty list for an xls (`extensions/spreadsheet/src/read/xls_extras.rs`). What it
spends: every extra and each picture's bytes, held with the rows until the reader is freed.

**Declined:**
- **A pull loop in the Novis half.** It costs a guest return and a Novis call per block on the request
  path, and rewrites every parser as a resumable machine (the paragraph above).
- **The whole file copied into the guest.** A 100 MB upload would cost 100 MB of guest memory beside
  the program's own copy.
- **A preopen for the uploaded file.** It is a grant to a parser of hostile bytes, and a range import
  on a lent value grants nothing ([`packaging/a-guest-has-no-ambient-authority`](packaging.md#packaging-a-guest-has-no-ambient-authority)).
- **Whole-sheet reads into one block.** A large sheet would cost its size; a batch of rows costs the
  same for every size.
- **A per-cell accessor.** [`core-classes/spreadsheet-bulk-boundary`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-bulk-boundary) declines it for good.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/spreadsheet-value-types`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-value-types), [`core-classes/spreadsheet-has-no-io`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-has-no-io), [`core-classes/decompression-bound`](core-classes.md#core-classes-decompression-bound), [`packaging/values-cross-as-handles`](packaging.md#packaging-values-cross-as-handles).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-spreadsheet-bulk-boundary"></a>

## A workbook crosses the boundary a batch at a time, never a cell at a time, and Excel's grid is the only limit it adds

`rule:core-classes/spreadsheet-bulk-boundary`

A workbook crosses the boundary a batch of rows at a time on write and a read-ahead block and a batch
of rows at a time on read, **never a cell at a time**, and Excel's own grid and limits are the only
limits the component adds. **There is no per-cell accessor, and none is added later**: a member that
would be called in a loop over the file's own contents costs the boundary, not the work — the same
refusal the image component makes ([`core-classes/image-pipeline`](core-classes.md#core-classes-image-pipeline)).

**Excel's limits throw, naming the limit and the place**: 1,048,576 rows and 16,384 columns, a row or
column index past them in a read file included; 32,767 characters in a cell; 65,490 cell formats;
8,192 characters in a formula; 255 characters in a defined name and in a chart or axis title.
**A sheet name** has 1 to 31 characters, none of `[ ] : * ? / \`, no control character, no `'`
first or last, and is not `History` in any case. One function checks it (`check_sheet_name` in
`extensions/spreadsheet/src/writer.rs`), for `Workbook::sheet`, a defined name's reference and a
chart's series range. **A defined name** in A1 or R1C1 form (`C3`, `R1C1`, `R`, `RC2`) throws. A merged range past the grid throws, and so does a record whose declared
length is past the bytes left. Every other bound is the request's: its memory and CPU caps hold the
guest ([`packaging/a-guest-runs-under-the-requests-budget`](packaging.md#packaging-a-guest-runs-under-the-requests-budget)), and the decompression bound holds
every inflated part ([`core-classes/decompression-bound`](core-classes.md#core-classes-decompression-bound)). **There is no cell cap.** A file's
declared dimensions and declared sizes are its author's numbers, so no member trusts them, not even as
a hint: memory is measured as it is spent.

- **Memory:** a batch of rows on each side of the boundary, never the sheet. Each crossing is charged
  to the request while it is converted (`crates/nvs-ext/src/call.rs`'s module doc).

**On disk.** Every limit above throws: the writer's in `extensions/spreadsheet/src/`, and the
reader's under `extensions/spreadsheet/src/read/`.

**Declined:**
- **A cell cap with its own knob, read from the declared dimensions.** A streamed read holds a batch
  whatever the sheet's size, so a cap would refuse large files that cost nothing, and the dimensions
  it would read are the attacker's to write. The request's memory cap is the bound that measures.
- **A per-cell accessor.** Called in a loop over a sheet, its cost is the boundary crossed once per
  cell.
- **Whole sheets as one block.** It holds the sheet, which a batch does not.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/image-pipeline`](core-classes.md#core-classes-image-pipeline), [`core-classes/image-pixel-cap`](core-classes.md#core-classes-image-pixel-cap), [`core-classes/spreadsheet-has-no-io`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-has-no-io).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-spreadsheet-evaluation-and-roster"></a>

## The roster reads xlsx, xlsm, xlsb, xls, ods and CSV and writes xlsx and CSV, a macro is never written, and nothing evaluates until the program calls evaluate

`rule:core-classes/spreadsheet-evaluation-and-roster`

The format roster is **read-wide and write-narrow**. xlsx reads and writes. CSV reads and writes through
the same classes, parsed and formatted by `Core\Csv`. xlsm reads its data, with its macros listed and
inert, and **is never written**: a filled xlsm template gives xlsx with no VBA part. xlsb and xls
(BIFF8) read and do not write, because a writer for a 1997 binary format is legacy nothing should
produce. ods reads and writes, from the same `Workbook` calls as xlsx, by our own writer, which holds
the workbook until `finish()` ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-writes-as-a-stream`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-writes-as-a-stream)). Template fill is in
the first wave ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-template-fill`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-template-fill)), because it is the workflow behind most
real exports.

**The crates**, each pinned and pure Rust, built for `wasm32-wasip2`, on `deny.toml`'s allowlist and
with no C in the build. Every format is read by our own reader. For xlsx and xlsb, `calamine` keeps
one `String` per shared string, exposes no cell style, and owns the `Read + Seek` a reader resource
must keep its place in between calls. For xls and ods it is the crate that fails to build: its
release on a `quick-xml` with no open advisory needs a `zip` that pulls in `typed-path`, which does
not build for `wasm32-wasip2` on stable Rust, and its release that builds carries `quick-xml`'s two
open advisories, which `deny.toml` refuses. Its replacement is our reader of the compound file and
BIFF8 records for xls, and of `content.xml` for ods. `zip` with `deflate`
only, and `miniz_oxide` or `flate2` on its pure-Rust backend, frame and inflate the archive;
`crc32fast` checks it; `quick-xml` reads and writes the XML; `itoa` and `ryu` write numbers. The
writer, the template filler and the number-format renderer are our own. A crate that fails to build
for `wasm32-wasip2` is replaced by its nearest pure-Rust equivalent, and this fragment names the
replacement. `rust_xlsxwriter` is a source of chart XML and of Excel-made fixtures, never a
dependency; `umya-spreadsheet` and `ironcalc` are not dependencies.

**Nothing evaluates implicitly** — not on read, and not on write, where a formula cell is written with
its cached result when the program gave one and the workbook is flagged to recalculate when opened. A
read formula cell is its stored result, and `{formulas: true}` gives the `Formula` with that result as
its `cached`, so the program can tell the author's claim from the cell's text
([`core-classes/spreadsheet-value-types`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-value-types)).

**`Reader::evaluate(): array<{cell: tainted string, kind: string, text: tainted string}>`** computes on
request. It computes every formula cell of every sheet once, in the guest, in dependency order, and
returns what it could not compute: `cell` as `Sheet!A1`, `kind` as `'function'` (a function outside
the set, with its name), `'reference'` (another workbook, a missing sheet, a 3D reference, a union, an
intersection, an array constant, or a result of more than one cell, with the reference), `'circular'`
(with the formula) or `'token'` (formula text the evaluator cannot read, or a formula the reader could
not decode). A test asserts that list is empty, the visibility rule the PDF component applies to
dropped CSS ([`core-classes/pdf-css-subset`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-css-subset)). After it, each `rows()` reads a formula cell as its
computed result, through the read table and the cell's number format, and `formulas: true` gives that
result as the `cached`. A cell it did not compute keeps its stored result, and a cell that reads it
reads that result. Every format feeds it: xlsx formula text (a shared formula moved to each cell),
xls and xlsb tokens through the token decoder, and ods OpenFormula through the translator. A CSV has
no formulas and returns `[]`.

- **Security.** It does no I/O and follows nothing. An external reference, `INDIRECT` and `OFFSET`
  are listed. It runs under the request's CPU and memory caps. A chain of 20,000 cells computes, and
  a cycle of any length is listed, because the order is walked with an explicit stack.
- **Memory.** One value per non-empty cell of every worksheet, in a sparse grid, so `A:A` walks only
  stored cells; the parsed formulas and the order. Per request, freed with the reader.
- **Latency.** One guest call, growing with the cells and the references. No existing read path
  pays anything until a program calls it.
- **Excel's behaviour.** Numbers are `f64`, and coercion and error values follow Excel. Text
  converts to a number when it is a number, a percentage, an ISO date or a clock time, and is
  `#VALUE!` otherwise, so a date in a locale's own order (`1/15/2024`) is `#VALUE!` here, because
  the result would depend on the machine. An unknown name is `#NAME?`. Defined names and structured
  references (`Table[Column]`, `[#This Row]`, `[#Data]`, `[#All]`, `[#Headers]`, `[#Totals]`)
  resolve, and a sheet-qualified name reads only that sheet's names.
- **Bounds.** Parentheses and calls more than 64 deep, a tree more than 512 nodes deep, or more
  than 4,096 operators and calls in one formula are `token`. A name chain more than 64 deep is
  `circular`. `ROW`, `COLUMN`, `ROWS` and `COLUMNS` read no cells, so `=ROWS(A1:A9)` in `A1` is not
  circular. `IF`, `IFERROR`, `IFNA`, `IFS` and `SWITCH` evaluate only what they take, so a function
  outside the set in a branch not taken is not listed. `SUBTOTAL` with a code from 1 to 11 over a
  range with a hidden row is listed, because the file does not say whether a filter hid it.

**The function set** is one table, `extensions/spreadsheet/src/eval/functions.rs`, and a test gives
each function a case:
- Math and statistics: `ABS`, `AVERAGE`, `AVERAGEIF`, `AVERAGEIFS`, `CEILING`, `CEILING.MATH`,
  `COUNT`, `COUNTA`, `COUNTBLANK`, `COUNTIF`, `COUNTIFS`, `EXP`, `FLOOR`, `FLOOR.MATH`, `INT`, `LN`,
  `LOG`, `LOG10`, `MAX`, `MAXIFS`, `MEDIAN`, `MIN`, `MINIFS`, `MOD`, `PI`, `POWER`, `PRODUCT`,
  `ROUND`, `ROUNDDOWN`, `ROUNDUP`, `SIGN`, `SQRT`, `SUBTOTAL` (codes 1 to 11 and 101 to 111), `SUM`,
  `SUMIF`, `SUMIFS`, `SUMPRODUCT`, `TRUNC`.
- Logic: `AND`, `FALSE`, `IF`, `IFERROR`, `IFNA`, `IFS`, `NOT`, `OR`, `SWITCH`, `TRUE`, `XOR`.
- Information: `ISBLANK`, `ISERR`, `ISERROR`, `ISEVEN`, `ISLOGICAL`, `ISNA`, `ISNUMBER`, `ISODD`,
  `ISTEXT`, `NA`.
- Text: `CHAR`, `CLEAN`, `CODE`, `CONCAT`, `CONCATENATE`, `EXACT`, `FIND`, `LEFT`, `LEN`, `LOWER`,
  `MID`, `PROPER`, `REPLACE`, `REPT`, `RIGHT`, `SEARCH`, `SUBSTITUTE`, `TEXT` (through the
  number-format renderer), `TEXTJOIN`, `TRIM`, `UPPER`, `VALUE`. Lengths and positions count UTF-16
  units, as Excel's do.
- Lookup: `CHOOSE`, `COLUMN`, `COLUMNS`, `HLOOKUP`, `INDEX`, `MATCH`, `ROW`, `ROWS`, `VLOOKUP`,
  `XLOOKUP`.
- Date and time: `DATE`, `DATEDIF`, `DAY`, `DAYS`, `EDATE`, `EOMONTH`, `HOUR`, `MINUTE`, `MONTH`,
  `SECOND`, `TIME`, `WEEKDAY`, `YEAR`.

`TODAY`, `NOW`, `RAND` and `RANDBETWEEN` are out, because the result would depend on when or how often
the program reads. `INDIRECT` and `OFFSET` are out, because they make a reference from data. These and
every function outside the table are listed. A function of the set given an input on which it cannot
match Excel is listed for that cell, and never computed differently.

**On disk.** Every format the roster reads (`extensions/spreadsheet/src/read/`) and writes
(`extensions/spreadsheet/src/writer.rs`, `extensions/spreadsheet/src/ods/`, and CSV in
`extensions/spreadsheet/nvs/`). The evaluator is `extensions/spreadsheet/src/eval/`, fed by
`extensions/spreadsheet/src/read/evaluate.rs`.


**Declined:**
- **Evaluating formulas on read.** Recalculating on open turns reading an attacker's upload into
  running the attacker's program ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-has-no-io`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-has-no-io)).
- **An option to compute `TODAY` and `NOW` from a given instant.** A program that needs one fills a
  cell with the instant.
- **Writing xls, xlsb or xlsm.** Legacy and binary formats nothing should produce, and a macro-enabled
  format whose only purpose over xlsx is the macros.
- **`umya-spreadsheet` for template fill.** It loads the whole workbook into an editable model
  ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-template-fill`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-template-fill)).

<sub>See also [`core-classes/spreadsheet-formula-is-a-value`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-formula-is-a-value), [`core-classes/spreadsheet-output-is-inert`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-output-is-inert), [`core-classes/pdf-css-subset`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-css-subset).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-spreadsheet-output-is-inert"></a>

## The writer and the template filler embed no executable content and no entropy, so equal input gives byte-equal output

`rule:core-classes/spreadsheet-output-is-inert`

The writer emits no macros, no embedded executables and no launch-shaped content; hyperlinks exist
only where the program wrote them.

**A reference the program writes stays in the workbook.** `Workbook::define` and a chart's series
range go through one reference parser (`extensions/spreadsheet/src/reference.rs`): an optional sheet
name, quoted as Excel quotes one, then `!`, then a cell, a range, whole columns (`$A:$C`) or whole
rows (`$1:$3`), each with or without `$`. A series range takes no whole columns or rows. The sheet
name follows the sheet name rule ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-bulk-boundary`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-bulk-boundary)). Another workbook
(`[other.xlsx]Shop!A1`), a DDE call (`cmd|'/c calc'!A0`), a URL, a function, an R1C1 reference and
a second sheet name throw `LogicError`, so neither DDE nor an external link reaches the file
through a name or a chart. A name whose sheet the workbook never adds throws at `finish()`, naming
the name and the sheet.

It embeds **no timestamps and no generator entropy** — document properties carry fixed dates unless
the program sets them, archive entries a fixed time, and no output depends on a map's order — so equal
input gives byte-equal output, for a write and for a template fill alike, and a document test is a
byte comparison. This is the same rule the PDF writer holds ([`core-classes/pdf-output-is-inert`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-output-is-inert)),
and it exists for the same reason: a test that cannot compare bytes ends up comparing nothing.

The component's tests owe a filled `.xlsm` template whose output a scanner finds no `vbaProject`
part in, and the same input written twice and filled twice, each pair compared byte for byte.

**On disk.** The writer (`extensions/spreadsheet/src/writer.rs`) and the template filler
(`extensions/spreadsheet/src/template/`) both hold the rule, and `extensions/spreadsheet/tests/excel.rs`
reads what each makes back through two readers. `extensions/spreadsheet/tests/write.rs` and
`chart.rs` hold the reference parser to its forms.

**Declined:**
- **A constant or a formula as a defined name's value**, such as `0.2` or `SUM(Shop!A1:A9)`. A
  name's value is the one place a formula would be written without `Formula`, and a formula there is
  where DDE and external links hide. `Formula` is the one way to write a formula, and a constant goes
  in a cell the name points to.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/pdf-output-is-inert`](core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-output-is-inert), [`core-classes/spreadsheet-evaluation-and-roster`](core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-evaluation-and-roster).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-net-one-api-three-transports"></a>

## `Core\Net` is one class over TCP, UDP and Unix sockets, reached through five entry points that park on the runtime's own reactor

`rule:core-classes/net-one-api-three-transports`

`Core\Net` is the whole socket surface: one class over three transports, TCP, UDP and Unix-domain
sockets. A program reaches them through
five entry points — an outbound TCP connection, a listening TCP socket, a bound UDP socket, an
outbound Unix-domain connection and a listening Unix-domain socket — and accepting is a member on the
listener rather than a sixth way in.

**No entry point decides between transports by reading its argument.** A host and a socket path are
separate members taking separately-typed arguments, so [`security/a-path-is-not-a-url`](security.md#security-a-path-is-not-a-url)'s refusal —
no member dispatches on the textual content of a path — holds by construction rather than by a check.
That is why the surface is five members and not two: a single connect taking `"unix://…"` or
`"tcp://…"` would be one function distinguished by a prefix, and the separate member is the security
property.

Every one of those sockets parks on the runtime's own reactor. `crates/nvs-host/src/net.rs` is the
contract they share — a `Read` and a `Write` that hand the core back instead of blocking it — and
`crates/nvs-host/src/reactor.rs` is its readiness half. A second event loop is never the answer: it
would be a second poll structure whose fairness, shutdown, deadline and drain semantics must be made
to agree with the reactor's by hand, and whose disagreements appear only under load, which is what
[`concurrency/one-scheduler`](concurrency.md#concurrency-one-scheduler) refuses for the scheduler on the same ground. A shape that cannot be
expressed over the reactor is cut, not given a loop of its own.

The connected transports answer a `Read` and a `Write` shaped like every other stream in the language.
A datagram socket does not, because it has no stream to read: it sends and receives whole messages,
addressed one at a time.

**Memory:** each open socket costs one reactor registration, held by the request that opened it
([`core-classes/net-a-socket-does-not-outlive-its-request`](core-classes.md#core-classes-net-a-socket-does-not-outlive-its-request)).

**Declined:**
- **A stream-shaped surface where one member opens any transport.** It is PHP's shape, and the
  argument's text would decide what gets opened, which [`security/a-path-is-not-a-url`](security.md#security-a-path-is-not-a-url) forbids.
- **A second event loop for the sockets a program opens.** Two poll structures must be made to agree
  by hand and disagree only under load ([`concurrency/one-scheduler`](concurrency.md#concurrency-one-scheduler)).
- **A member for a connected pair of anonymous sockets.** [`core-classes/net-has-no-socket-pair`](core-classes.md#core-classes-net-has-no-socket-pair).

<sub>See also [`security/net-listen-is-a-separate-grant-from-net-connect`](security.md#security-net-listen-is-a-separate-grant-from-net-connect), [`security/a-path-is-not-a-url`](security.md#security-a-path-is-not-a-url), [`concurrency/one-scheduler`](concurrency.md#concurrency-one-scheduler), [`core-classes/net-udp-carries-no-reliability-layer`](core-classes.md#core-classes-net-udp-carries-no-reliability-layer).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-net-a-socket-does-not-outlive-its-request"></a>

## A `Core\Net` socket closes with the request that opened it, so there is no persistent connection and no pool across requests

`rule:core-classes/net-a-socket-does-not-outlive-its-request`

A socket opened through `Core\Net` closes with the request that opened it. There is no persistent
connection, no pool held across requests and no handle a later request can find, which is
[`security/no-cross-request-state`](security.md#security-no-cross-request-state) applied to sockets, the subsystem where a persistent connection
is the most tempting shape: no member opens one. PHP's `pfsockopen` maps to `Core\Net::connect` with its
persistent half dropped.

**Memory:** one reactor registration per open socket, attributable to the request that opened it and
released with its arena. The process holds one registration per socket **in flight** and nothing per
socket served, which is the O(in-flight) bound that separates a cost from a leak.

A program that wants a connection to survive a request wants a store, and the stores are the ones
already granted by name — [`config/cache-shared-is-the-grant-over-the-configured-store`](config.md#config-cache-shared-is-the-grant-over-the-configured-store)'s shared
cache and [`core-classes/db-one-api`](core-classes.md#core-classes-db-one-api)'s database — where the endpoint is an operator's and the
lifetime is the runtime's.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/net-one-api-three-transports`](core-classes.md#core-classes-net-one-api-three-transports), [`security/no-cross-request-state`](security.md#security-no-cross-request-state), [`programs/memory-priority`](programs.md#programs-memory-priority).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-net-udp-carries-no-reliability-layer"></a>

## A datagram socket sends and receives messages and offers no ordering, retransmission or acknowledgement above them

`rule:core-classes/net-udp-carries-no-reliability-layer`

A `Core\Net` datagram socket sends and receives messages, reports what it sent and what arrived, and
offers nothing above that: no ordering, no retransmission, no fragmentation and no acknowledgement. A
datagram that is lost is lost, and a program that cannot tolerate that wants TCP.

The refusal is written down because the pressure to add "just a retry" is constant and its result is
always the same — a reliability layer nobody specified, whose failure modes belong to the library
while the timing budget it spends belongs to the program. A protocol that genuinely provides reliable
datagrams is a protocol, placed by [`core-api/tier-placement`](core-api.md#core-api-tier-placement) like any other, and Tier 0 is not
where it lands.

A program that builds ordering or retries over this surface is making that choice explicitly, which is
the point: the trade is visible in the program rather than hidden in a member's contract.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/net-one-api-three-transports`](core-classes.md#core-classes-net-one-api-three-transports), [`core-api/tier-placement`](core-api.md#core-api-tier-placement).</sub>

<a id="core-classes-net-has-no-socket-pair"></a>

## There is no `Core\Net` socket pair: PHP's `stream_socket_pair` is dropped, because no process boundary can receive one

`rule:core-classes/net-has-no-socket-pair`

`Core\Net` has no member that opens a connected pair of anonymous sockets, and PHP's
`stream_socket_pair` is a `dropped` row. A socket pair exists to be handed to a forked child. Novis has
no fork, and the one process boundary it has is an isolate, which shares nothing
([`security/isolate-shares-nothing`](security.md#security-isolate-shares-nothing)) and so cannot receive a descriptor. A member for it would have
no caller, and a PHP function with no Novis answer is a `dropped` row, never a member written to fill a
hole.

<sub>See also [`core-classes/net-one-api-three-transports`](core-classes.md#core-classes-net-one-api-three-transports), [`security/isolate-shares-nothing`](security.md#security-isolate-shares-nothing).</sub>
